artigo.texto: At least 130 civil society organisations have urged the UN carbon market body to suspend further issuance, transfer and use of credits linked to a cookstove project in Myanmar. The project became the first to receive carbon credits under Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement in February 2026. The groups have raised concerns over the reliability of emissions reductions, independent verification, human rights safeguards and possible financial benefits to Myanmar's military authorities. Earlier analyses cited by the groups estimated that the project was over-credited by factors of 14 under the Clean Development Mechanism and seven under Article 6.4. The appeal comes as the Article 6.4 Supervisory Body meets in Bonn from October 5 to 9, with campaigners demanding an independent investigation. At least 130 civil society organisations, networks and other stakeholders have called on a United Nations carbon market body to suspend credits linked to a cookstove project in Myanmar, the first to receive carbon credits under the Paris Agreement’s new carbon market mechanism. The groups have urged the Supervisory Body of the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM) to immediately halt any further issuance, transfer or use of credits associated with the project, known as PoA 10471. Their demand comes as the body holds its 23rd meeting in Bonn, Germany, from October 5 to 9, 2026, where members are discussing how the new carbon market will operate, including the approval, issuance and tracking of credits. In an open letter dated October 6, 2026, the organisations raised concerns about the project's environmental integrity, monitoring and verification processes, human rights safeguards and the participation of local communities. They also called for an independent and detailed assessment of the project. The signatories include the Global Forest Coalition, Biomass Action Network's Asia Pacific Working Group, the Korean Federation for Environmental Movement, North American Climate, Conservation and Environment, Women's Earth and Climate Action Network and Bio Vision Africa. Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement establishes a UN-supervised carbon crediting mechanism that allows verified emissions reductions from projects in one country to be credited and potentially transferred to buyers in another. Rules governing the mechanism were finalised at the 29th Conference of the Parties (COP 29) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change in Baku, Azerbaijan, in 2024. The Myanmar cookstove project, managed by South Korea's Climate Change Center (CCC), became the first project to receive credits under the mechanism in February 2026. The project involves distributing fuel-efficient Envirofit M5000 cookstoves to households in Myanmar. According to the project, the stoves can reduce household firewood consumption by more than 50 per cent, potentially lowering emissions and reducing pressure on local fuelwood resources. The UN said credits authorised for use in South Korea could be transferred to Korean entities for compliance under the country's emissions trading system, contributing to its nationally determined contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement. The remaining credits would be used by Myanmar towards its own climate commitments. However, civil society groups have questioned whether the emissions reductions claimed by the project can be reliably verified, particularly given Myanmar's political and security situation. Article 6.4 has taken years to build, and its credibility rests on the confidence that its credits would represent real, verifiable emissions reductions, said Trishant Dev, deputy programme manager, Climate Change and Green Economy unit for Delhi-based think tank Centre for Science and Environment. “Its first issuance is therefore a test of the system itself. When serious integrity concerns are raised, the Supervisory Body cannot wave them through. It must examine the evidence in the open and show that the mechanism’s safeguards actually work, something necessary to maintain trust and confidence in a UN-led carbon market,” he said. The project was designed and registered before Myanmar's military coup in February 2021 but continued operating during almost the entire monitoring period used to calculate its first Article 6.4 credits. That period ran from January 2021 to May 2022. The project operated in parts of Myanmar affected by violence, displacement and reports of human rights abuses following the military takeover. According to the civil society letter, the project was implemented and monitored for almost the entire 17-month period by the Dry Zone Greening Department and other authorities operating under military control. The groups questioned whether reliable monitoring and independent verification were possible under these conditions. They also raised concerns about the financial arrangements associated with the project. The letter said there was insufficient publicly available information about who had received financial benefits from the project. It warned that Myanmar's military authorities might have benefited, or could continue to benefit, from funding arrangements and credit transfers associated with the project, first under the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and subsequently under Article 6.4. The letter did not establish that such financial benefits had been received. The groups also questioned why the project's monitoring documents had not adequately addressed the changes in Myanmar's political and security conditions or their possible effects on emissions reductions. According to the letter, verification was conducted remotely, without site inspections because of security risks. The process relied on just 22 online interviews, only two of which were with women, despite the project having distributed nearly one million cookstoves. artigo.texto: HAILEY, Idaho — Blaine County commissioners passed an emergency moratorium pausing data center permitting, giving the county 182 days to draft new rules as artificial intelligence drives growing demand for the facilities. County Commissioner Lindsay Mollineaux said no influx of data center permit applications has hit Blaine County yet, but she is not going to wait around for it to happen. "I remember reading about things growing up and thinking, oh, that's never going to happen in Idaho. That's not the world anymore," Mollineaux said. Bannock and Kootenai counties already have moratoriums in place on data centers, and Mollineaux said she expects more counties to follow suit soon. She pointed to what other states have already experienced as a signal for what could be ahead. "Just like other states have seen potentially a big wave, we might be next, and so again, you want some time to get everything in order," Mollineaux said. The commissioners agreed, adopting the emergency moratorium to pause permitting until the Planning and Zoning Department can draft an ordinance to address data centers. Outside the courthouse, resident Alexis Limburg told me laws governing data centers should be in place before they are needed. "Before anything can come in without people really agreeing to it, you know, they should have a chance today to put those laws in place," Limburg said. Resident Heidi Bynum gave her public comment during the meeting. "Just say nix, I just wish you could just say nix," Bynum said. Mollineaux said other states have taken the lead in setting rules and guidelines for data centers, but in Idaho, it is up to each county — or even each municipality — to figure it out. "And so it's put, I think, a huge burden on our counties and cities to really think about things. We never thought we would have to think about," Mollineaux said. Mollineaux said the moratorium gives the county time to update its code and hold public conversations before anyone moves forward under old rules. "While we have time to sort to get everything together and update the code and have those public conversations, there's not the opportunity for someone's going to come in under the old rules, which we've already decided you don't need to be tightened up," Mollineaux said. She said the county's work on data center regulations is only just beginning. "And so my anticipation is, this will be the start of the conversation, but not the end of it," Mollineaux said. The county now has 182 days to draw up a plan to address data centers. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. artigo.texto: Cooling battery cells directly in liquid creates an engineering challenge: keeping that liquid away from electrical equipment. BYD has filed a patent application for a two-chamber cabinet that separates submerged battery modules from electronics and routes their connections through the upper part of the liquid-filled compartment. The China National Intellectual Property Administration published the application, numbered CN 122868832 A, on October 5, 2026. Filed in March 2025, it describes battery cabinets and energy storage equipment that use dielectric fluid to absorb heat directly from the modules. The design places electrical equipment in a dry upper chamber and battery modules in a wet lower chamber. Its focus is the boundary between those spaces, where connections must pass through without allowing cooling liquid to reach components intended to remain dry. Bringing cooling liquid directly to the cells Many battery systems remove heat through an indirect cooling arrangement. Liquid circulates inside aluminum cold plates positioned against battery modules, drawing heat through the cell casing and materials between the cells and plates. Immersion cooling changes that heat-transfer route. Battery modules sit directly in a non-conductive fluid, allowing heat to pass from their wetted surfaces into the surrounding liquid. This shortens the thermal path, but containing the fluid becomes part of the cabinet’s design. Electrical equipment and connection points that are not intended for immersion still require protection from the liquid. More from Transportation See All BYD’s application specifies dielectric cooling fluids, including hydrocarbon- or ester-based formulations. These fluids provide electrical insulation while cooling the submerged modules. Moving connections higher to reduce pressure The proposed cabinet divides the battery and its electrical equipment into two isolated compartments. The lower chamber holds the immersed modules, while the upper chamber houses electrical components outside the liquid volume. Electrical and signal connections pass through the upper portion of the wet chamber before entering the dry compartment. The arrangement avoids routing those connections through the floor or deeper sections of the liquid-filled chamber. That positioning matters because hydrostatic pressure increases with depth. A sealing interface near the top experiences less liquid pressure than one farther down, reducing the pressure acting on the boundary between compartments. The design therefore combines an insulating fluid with a physical separation between cooling and electrical equipment. The cabinet’s layout addresses how connections cross that separation while keeping sensitive components outside the main liquid volume. A storage cabinet awaiting commercial plans The application covers battery cabinets and energy storage equipment. It does not identify a passenger-vehicle application, so the filing does not establish that BYD intends to use this arrangement in an electric car. Existing systems use different cooling layouts. BYD’s MC Cube-T specifies liquid cooling, while CATL’s EnerOne and EnerC storage systems use cooling plates outside their battery modules. CATL’s Qilin vehicle battery places a liquid-cooling plate between adjacent cells. BYD’s filing instead places the modules inside the cooling fluid itself. The application remains under substantive examination, and the company has not announced commercial production plans for the proposed cabinet.

artigo.texto: Columbia Planning and Zoning discusses electric grid needs as it considers data center rules COLUMBIA, Mo. (KMIZ) A survey conducted by Columbia's Planning and Zoning Commission found that a majority of respondents believe the city should not build a data center. But as interest in technology grows, city officials are working to determine what regulations would be needed if a data center were proposed. Patrick Zenner, Columbia's director of Development Services, said the goal is to establish guidelines before any potential development moves forward. "We are simply and merely trying to make sure we aren't caught flat-footed without a set of regulations to provide guidance. The ultimate decision here, if we do adopt anything, lies with council," Zenner said during the meeting. The City Council on May 18 passed a one-year moratorium on data center applications and development. The committee has until next March to present its proposed rules and regulations to City Council. Electricity demand is one of the key concerns. According to the committees presentation, the city's historical peak electricity demand is about 290 megawatts, and many of its substations and circuits are already approaching capacity. Projects requiring more than 20 megawatts of electricity could require significant infrastructure upgrades, a city presentation says. Depending on where a project connects to the grid, even a smaller development requiring 5 megawatts could present challenges for the city’s electric utility. If Columbia's existing electricity supply cannot meet a data center's needs, developers may need to explore power purchase agreements to secure additional electricity. Zenner said Columbia already relies on electricity generated outside the city through the regional Midcontinent Independent System Operator. "We are purchasing off the grid from somewhere else. It's not generated here, and so we're buying wind from Kansas. And because it's part of the MISO grid, it's being credited to us even though we're not using that wind energy — we're not directly using that," Zenner said. The agreements could include a schedule for gradually increasing the amount of electricity purchased as demand grows. "Because it may come from multiple sources, like you may have a piece that comes from MISO, you may have another piece that comes from somewhere else," Zenner said. Zenner said any potential power arrangements for a data center would be handled through the city's utility department. Those upgrades could raise questions about who would pay for the additional infrastructure and how the city could protect existing utility customers from increased costs. Missouri regulators have approved a large-load power service tariff aimed at investor-owned utilities, including Ameren and Evergy. The tariff targets new customers with an expected ramp rate exceeding 75 megawatts. However, according to the presentation, no equivalent legislation is currently in effect for municipal utilities such as Columbia’s. Discussions about similar efforts are beginning ahead of the 2027 legislative session. City documents outline potential ways a data center could meet its electricity needs without placing additional strain on Columbia’s existing grid. It presents an option of generating electricity on site, while another would involve purchasing power from an off-site provider through a power purchase agreement. Under either scenario, the developer would also need a backup power plan to account for potential outages or disruptions, city documents say. The city is also considering how a data center could remain a utility customer even if it secures its own power supply. If a data center generates its own electricity on-site, one potential arrangement would involve the generation facilities eventually being owned by the city’s electric utility or Boone Electric. Officials claim that approach could create additional jobs in the area. If the developer instead purchases electricity through an off-site agreement, that contracted capacity could help the utility meet its peak demand obligations. The said the goal is to ensure a data center can meet its own power needs without placing additional strain on Columbia’s electric grid, while allowing the city and its utility customers to benefit from the development.

artigo.texto: The Maryland Public Service Commission has conditionally selected two transmission-connected energy storage projects totaling 440 MW for Energy Storage Capacity Credit awards under the first round of the state’s Next Generation Energy Act procurement. The Commission regulates public utilities in Maryland, and the storage procurement is designed to support financing by providing a more stable revenue stream against uncertainty in future PJM Interconnection capacity market prices. The Chalk Point Storage Project would provide 400 MW at the existing Chalk Point power plant site in Aquasco, Prince George’s County, while the 40 MW Jade Meadow III Battery Storage Project would be a combined solar-and-storage facility on a reclaimed coal mine in Barton, Garrett County. Together, the projects would provide 440 MW with four-hour durations under flat, 15-year award terms, with an estimated combined cost of 6.98 cents per month for a typical Maryland residential customer. Round 1 targeted 800 MW, while the Next Generation Energy Act requires at least two solicitations for a cumulative 1,600 MW of front-of-the-meter, transmission-connected energy storage with a minimum four-hour duration. The Commission selected Chalk Point and Jade Meadow III as the most cost-effective and highest-ranked remaining proposals after public and evidentiary hearings, while the 500 MW Oystercatcher Energy Storage Project was not selected. Both selected projects must still apply for Commission construction approval, and the Round 2 Request for Applications will be issued by January 1, 2027. artigo.texto: Canadian Solar Inc. has announced that its energy storage solutions business, e-STORAGE, has signed an agreement to supply and commission a 100 MW/200 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) for OX2’s Muswellbrook Solar Farm and Battery project in New South Wales, Australia. Shipments for the project are scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027, while commercial operations are targeted for the third quarter of 2028. The battery cells and SolBank systems will be manufactured at Canadian Solar’s own facilities, providing greater supply-chain visibility and quality control. Under the agreement, e-STORAGE will deliver an integrated energy storage solution based on its SolBank 3.0 battery containers, along with power conversion systems, plant controls and its proprietary EQ-S Energy Management System (EMS). The EMS has been developed in-house by e-STORAGE’s North American software team. The company will also undertake R1 grid connection studies, provide a hybrid power plant controller to coordinate the battery system with the co-located solar farm, and lead the overall integration and commissioning of the hybrid facility. The project is backed by a 20-year long-term service agreement (LTSA), covering hardware, proprietary software and long-term system performance under a single service arrangement. Located approximately 2.5 kilometres east of Muswellbrook, the solar-plus-storage facility will be developed on land at a former coal mine within the Hunter-Central Coast Renewable Energy Zone. The project comes as the Hunter region prepares for the retirement of aging coal-fired generation capacity in the early 2030s. The two-hour battery system is expected to store surplus solar generation during periods of high daytime output and dispatch electricity during evening peak-demand periods, supporting grid reliability as conventional thermal generation declines. Once operational, the BESS will support OX2’s long-term hybrid power purchase agreement for the project. By combining solar generation with dispatchable battery storage, the facility is designed to provide firmer renewable electricity while supporting the Hunter region’s transition away from coal-fired power. Steve Symons, Vice President of OX2 Australia, said the storage system would transform Muswellbrook into a hybrid facility capable of capturing solar power when available and supplying it when required by the grid. Jeff Roy, President of e-STORAGE, highlighted the growing role of battery storage in regions transitioning away from coal generation, adding that e-STORAGE’s integrated approach covers battery cells, energy management software and long-term servicing. artigo.texto: A revisão técnica do padrão corporativo Corporate Net-Zero Standard, conduzida pela Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), estabelece novos critérios de integridade para corporações que buscam neutralizar impactos climáticos. Sob as novas diretrizes regulatórias globais, mecanismos genéricos de compensação perdem prioridade em favor de intervenções diretas nas cadeias de suprimentos das próprias empresas. De acordo com análise apresentada por Rodrigo Oliveira, diretor-presidente da Green Mining e vice-presidente da Associação Brasileira de Empresas de Logística Reversa (ABELORE), essa orientação reposiciona o crédito de carbono gerado pela reciclagem como um instrumento central para neutralizar emissões residuais de embalagens nos setores de bens de consumo, varejo, cosméticos, higiene, e-commerce e alimentos. Segundo o executivo da entidade, a reformulação normativa atinge diretamente a governança ambiental de conglomerados que operam sob alta intensidade de empacotamento. Em pronunciamento institucional, a empresa de rastreabilidade logística sustenta que a compra de créditos climáticos tradicionais, desvinculada do ciclo produtivo dos resíduos descartados no pós-consumo, torna-se insuficiente para atender a investidores institucionais e reguladores internacionais. Para a organização, a redução de pegada ecológica nesses segmentos exige vinculação direta com a logística reversa e a substituição efetiva de matéria-prima virgem por materiais reaproveitados. Pressão do Escopo 3 na indústria de consumo Nos cálculos de inventários de gases de efeito estufa (GEE), a gestão de resíduos sólidos e materiais embalados concentra a maior parte do impacto ambiental fora dos limites fabris imediatos. Conforme expõe a Green Mining, os setores de comércio varejista e bens não duráveis registram o grosso de seu passivo ecológico no chamado Escopo 3. Esse parâmetro técnico abrange as fases de extração de insumos, frete logístico terceirizado, manuseio no ponto de venda e, de forma crítica, a destinação final dada pelo consumidor aos frascos, caixas e recipientes plásticos, metálicos, celulósicos ou de vidro. Na avaliação da entidade setorial, estratégias como redesign estrutural de recipientes, diminuição da espessura de invólucros plásticos, ampliação de modelos de refil e troca de insumos fósseis por componentes biodegradáveis diminuem expressivamente os inventários absolutos. Contudo, a Green Mining argumenta que essas medidas não eliminam a integralidade das emissões associadas à produção primária e ao frete de retorno. Mesmo diante de saltos de ecoeficiência industrial, persiste um volume residual contínuo de resíduos que demanda soluções de compensação aderentes à matriz de materiais de cada organização. Mecânica operacional do crédito lastreado em resíduos A tese defendida pela companhia estabelece que a integridade climática requer paridade entre o vetor de poluição e a ferramenta escolhida para mitigação. No entendimento manifestado pela diretoria da Green Mining, companhias que comercializam recipientes em larga escala cometem inconsistência metodológica quando tentam saldar passivos materiais exclusivamente via projetos florestais distantes ou iniciativas energéticas desconectadas do ecossistema de manufatura. - A coleta é auditada em pontos georreferenciados para garantir a adicionalidade do volume recuperado. - Pesagem e triagem são registradas eletronicamente para impedir duplicidade de notas ou contagem fictícia. - A homologação de transformadores industriais atesta o reprocessamento de insumos secundários. - O cálculo de carbono abatido compara o gasto energético da reciclagem contra a produção virgem primária. A alegação técnica da Green Mining pontua que o benefício mensurável desse modelo deriva da substituição da matéria-prima virgem — como bauxita no alumínio, areia e barrilha no vidro ou derivados de petróleo no polietileno — por insumos secundários que demandam fração sensivelmente menor de energia calorífica e elétrica durante o refundimento industrial. Ao documentar e auditar esse percurso de ponta a ponta, a companhia sustenta que a operação gera lastro técnico verificável para emissão de ativos ambientais. Gargalos estruturais da cadeia reversa brasileira O mercado brasileiro apresenta uma disparidade estrutural entre o volume de materiais descartados diariamente e a capacidade de reprocessamento das usinas nacionais. Dados setoriais defendidos pela assessoria da Green Mining ressaltam que o país detém uma das mais expressivas redes de reciclagem social do planeta, ancorada no trabalho de cooperativas e operadores autônomos. Apesar dessa capilaridade de campo, os índices gerais de retorno pós-consumo permanecem muito aquém do potencial de mitigação das cidades. Sob a ótica detalhada pela entidade, o valor de venda de materiais como vidro ou plásticos flexíveis não remunera adequadamente os custos agregados de frete, triagem mecanizada, formalização trabalhista e armazenamento intermediário. A Green Mining argumenta que o crédito de carbono gerado pela atividade opera como uma alavanca de capitalização privada capaz de cobrir o déficit financeiro de coleta nas municipalidades, viabilizando a inclusão socioprodutiva de catadores e a expansão de tecnologias de leitura óptica e rastreamento serial. Critérios de integridade e auditoria corporativa À medida que diretrizes internacionais como a SBTi intensificam as exigências de comprovação contra o greenwashing, fundos de investimento e comitês de auditoria passam a exigir comprovação de adicionalidade nos investimentos ambientais. Conforme postulado pelo relatório corporativo da Green Mining, compradores institucionais de crédito não se contentam mais com atestados estáticos de equivalência métrica; o foco migrou para a auditoria de processos que gerem benefícios econômicos e sociais comprováveis nas regiões impactadas. - Comprovação documental de que o material recolhido não seria absorvido sem o incentivo financeiro adicional.

artigo.texto: Verlume conclui testes hiperbáricos de sistema de bateria submarina de 500 kWh antes de implantação no Mar do Norte holandês A Verlume, especialista em baterias submarinas e sistemas de gerenciamento de energia com sede no Reino Unido, testou seu sistema modular de armazenamento de energia submarino de 500 kWh em Aberdeen antes de uma implantação planejada no Mar do Norte holandês, de acordo com a Offshore Energy. O sistema está previsto para se tornar a primeira bateria submarina formadora de rede co-localizada com energia eólica offshore após a instalação. A Verlume informou em 1º de outubro que havia concluído os testes hiperbáricos de seu invólucro submarino Orah na instalação de testes hiperbáricos da JFD em Aberdeen, um passo que a empresa descreveu como um importante marco de qualificação antes da implantação planejada do sistema no parque eólico offshore OranjeWind. Esse projeto está sendo desenvolvido pela RWE e pela TotalEnergies na costa holandesa. O sistema modular de armazenamento de energia submarino de 500 kWh foi projetado para fornecer suporte autônomo de rede para parques eólicos offshore. O Orah utiliza química de bateria atual e é gerenciado pela plataforma de gerenciamento de energia Axonn da Verlume. Segundo a empresa, essas tecnologias se combinam para formar uma solução modular de armazenamento de energia e suporte autônomo de rede destinada a ajudar a viabilizar sistemas de energia offshore mais flexíveis e resilientes. Com peso de 10 toneladas e dimensões de 7,2 metros de comprimento, 2,4 metros de largura e 2,4 metros de altura, o sistema é descrito como o maior vaso já testado no centro hiperbárico da JFD até o momento. O programa de testes submeteu o invólucro a um perfil de pressão controlado que representa seu ambiente operacional submarino pretendido. Ele se concentrou em três áreas críticas: qualificação de pressão e profundidade, integridade do invólucro e desempenho funcional sob pressão. Depois que o sistema completo de 85 toneladas for implantado no parque eólico offshore OranjeWind, ele representará a primeira bateria submarina formadora de rede co-localizada com energia eólica offshore. Este relatório fornece uma análise aprofundada do mercado de acumuladores elétricos de íons de lítio (exceto usados) nos Países Baixos, cobrindo tamanho de mercado, crescimento, demanda, oferta, fluxos comerciais, preços, cenário competitivo e previsões até 2035. O estudo é projetado para fabricantes, distribuidores, importadores, exportadores, investidores, equipes de compras, consultores e equipes de estratégia que precisam de uma visão consistente e orientada por dados da dinâmica do mercado e de uma definição analítica transparente do escopo do produto. Cobertura do Produto Acumuladores Elétricos de Íons de Lítio (Exceto Usados) abrange células e baterias secundárias de íons de lítio novas e não utilizadas, projetadas para armazenamento e fornecimento de energia elétrica, incluindo separadores, em formatos retangulares, quadrados, cilíndricos, prismáticos ou tipo bolsa. O escopo abrange acumuladores completos prontos para integração em equipamentos, bem como células individuais e módulos que fazem parte de um sistema de bateria maior. Acumuladores usados, gastos ou resíduos destinados à reciclagem ou descarte são excluídos. Incluídos - Acumuladores de íons de lítio com formato retangular ou quadrado - Acumuladores de íons de lítio com formato cilíndrico - Células e baterias prismáticas de íons de lítio - Células e baterias tipo bolsa de íons de lítio - Módulos e pacotes de baterias de íons de lítio - Acumuladores de íons de lítio com sistemas integrados de gerenciamento de bateria - Acumuladores de íons de lítio de alta densidade de energia para veículos elétricos - Acumuladores de íons de lítio com química de fosfato de ferro e lítio (LFP) Excluídos - Acumuladores de íons de lítio usados ou gastos para reciclagem - Células e baterias primárias de lítio (não recarregáveis) - Acumuladores elétricos de níquel-cádmio - Acumuladores elétricos de níquel-metal hidreto - Acumuladores elétricos de chumbo-ácido - Carregadores e equipamentos de teste para baterias de íons de lítio Cobertura do Relatório e Módulos Analíticos O relatório combina a base padrão de estatísticas de mercado com capítulos estratégicos úteis para planejamento comercial, decisões de sourcing, entrada no mercado, monitoramento de concorrentes e priorização de portfólio. - Exportações, importações, balança comercial, dependência de importação e principais corredores comerciais - Níveis de preço, corredores de preço, efeitos de especificação e lógica comercial de preços - artigo.texto: The Alabama Public Service Commission voted on Tuesday to keep a ‘deemed approved’ process that lets Alabama Power’s electricity contracts with the largest data centers take effect without a vote of the commission. The new rule extends the review period from 10 days to 90 days, but retains the previous rule of automatic approval for Alabama Power data center contracts if the commission fails to make a decision within 90 days. Energy Alabama advocated for a public vote on all applicable data center contracts in written comments this summer. “For three decades, rules built for manufacturers let contracts take effect without a vote of the Commission. Data centers on this scale are a different animal,” Daniel Tait, executive director of Energy Alabama, said. “Ninety days is better than ten, but silence still counts as yes. A contract this big should never take effect because nobody voted. Alabamians deserve to see their regulators decide, in public.” The Alabama Attorney General's Office also submitted comments on August 6, calling for a vote by commission members on contracts between Alabama Power and data centers. “The elected and appointed members of the Alabama Public Service Commission must actively participate in the decisions of the commission by voting on large load contracts, especially when the matter involves an assessment of public benefits or a determination of the public interest,” Olivia Martin, division chief of consumer interest with the AG’s Office, said in August. The new rule requires Alabama Power to file a public petition naming the data center customer and its parent companies, the city or county where the facility will be built, and the maximum amount of power it has contracted for. Other aspects of the contract would be confidential. All three members of the commission said they wanted future commissioners to vote on the contracts, but still approved a “deemed approved” process where contracts could be approved if the commission doesn’t vote within 90 days of the petition being submitted. According to the rule approved at Tuesday’s meeting, “Contracts submitted under this process shall be approved or disapproved through a commission vote within 90 days of the submission of the filing of the petition. If the commission fails to vote within 90 days, the petition is deemed approved.” “I feel strongly that we should take a public vote as a commission on data centers. We should not follow the deemed approved process that we’ve been following for a number of years,” Cynthia Almond, Public Service Commission President, said. “It should be a very public process we go through, I believe, because the public is very interested in this, very concerned about it. If we don’t take a public vote, that to me is not doing our job.” Almond and other commission members, Jeremy Oden and Chip Beeker, also voted for the new rule. Oden and Beeker both lost their Republican primary races in May. The commission is set to expand to seven seats in January 2027 under a new law passed in the 2026 session. artigo.texto: NYE COUNTY (KTNV) — Nye County commissioners passed new rules that expand the county's regulation on data centers. You might remember the county recently passed a permanent ban on new data center construction in August — but that regulation only applied to the Pahrump Valley. (A lawsuit challenging that ban has since been filed.) Additional rules passed on Thursday apply to data centers that would be built anywhere else in the county, which is Nevada's largest by geographic area at approximately 18,000 square miles. The nearly-200-page ordinance contains a number of provisions to regulate any future data center construction, including: - Requiring data center developers to get a special use permit and development agreement - Banning the construction of data centers in all residential and agricultural districts - Requiring any developer applying to build a data center to cover infrastructure costs, including the cost of energy - Prohibiting data centers from using more than 1.5 acre-feet of water, per acre, per year - Banning the use of evaporative cooling or release of process air emissions (meaning a data center could not release gas or vapor byproducts into the atmosphere) The ordinance is expected to take effect on Oct. 28. Watch Nye County residents react to the data center ban approved in August: As locals continue to raise concerns about data centers in Southern Nevada, Channel 13 has worked to get answers that help you understand what's happening in your community. Our five-part "Data vs. Desert" series delves into the issues at the center of this discussion and addresses concerns you've shared with us. Find out more at ktnv.com/datacenters.

artigo.texto: Judge dismisses DC Blox lawsuit challenging Metro Nashville’s actions surrounding proposed data center near zoo The judge said some of the claims were too unclear about what rights DC Blox said Metro took away. What This Story Is About - The DC Blox lawsuit that challenged Metro Nashville’s actions surrounding a proposed data center has been dismissed and its subsequent request for a preliminary injunction has also been denied. Why It Matters - DC Blox was vying for a property next to the Nashville Zoo for a data center that sparked a petition with more than 600,000 signatures as well as responses from local celebrities. What Happens Next - The judge said DC Blox can try again with a clearer explanation, within 21 days by filing either “an answer or a motion to dismiss” the amended complaint. For Context Catch Up NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - The DC Blox lawsuit that challenged Metro Nashville’s actions surrounding a proposed data center has been dismissed and its subsequent request for a preliminary injunction has also been denied. In August, DC Blox sued Metro Nashville in federal court and challenged the city’s data-center moratorium and its decision to halt permit processing for the company’s project that was proposed next to the Nashville Zoo. DC Blox alleged that the site had operated as a data center under a previous tenant, Asurion, and claimed Metro’s actions violated due process, equal protection and constitutional protections against taking property without just compensation. Overall, DC Blox brought nine claims to the judge. Four federal constitutional claims and five claims seeking declaratory relief which include the following: - Substantive due process: The Moratorium reportedly interfered irrationally with DC Blox’s protected property, use, pre-existing-use or vested permit rights - Equal protection: Metro allegedly treated DC Blox differently from similar developers, including RadiusDC, without a rational basis. - Procedural due process: DC Blox claims metro place their applications on hold despite asserted protected rights without adequate process - Takings: The moratorium allegedly took DC Blox’s property rights without just compensation - Pre-existing use: a declaration that DC Blox asserted protected data-center use under Tennessee law had not been terminated - Vested permits: A declaration that DC Blox’s July 17 application vested rights and should be judge under the law in effect when filed - BZA Authority: A declaration that the amended moratorium was invalid because it was not referred back to the planning commission for review - Validity of the moratorium: A declaration that the amended moratorium was invalid because it was not referred back to the Planning Commission for review - State-law preemption: A declaration that the moratorium was preempted by Tennessee’s vested-property-rights statute. Of the nine claims, the judge dismissed three. The judge said some of the claims were too unclear about what rights DC Blox said Metro took away. The judge said DC Blox can try again with a clearer explanation, within 21 days by filing either “an answer or a motion to dismiss” the amended complaint. Councilmember Courtney Johnston said that Metro has both the right and the responsibility to determine appropriate land uses through its legislative and zoning processes. “DC BLOX had every right to challenge those decisions in court. They did. This was the result,” Johnston said in a Facebook post. Read the full lawsuits and claims below. Copyright 2026 WSMV. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Starpointe data center developer paid for flights, lunch for township supervisors A developer paid for an out-of-state trip for local officials who are considering its conditional use permit application for a proposed seven-building data center campus and attached natural gas power plant in Starpointe Business Park near Burgettstown. Kate Nolan Bryden, the project lead from Dallas, Texas-based Prime Data Centers LCC, testified in a Wednesday night hearing that the company paid for airline tickets and lunch for at least two of the three Hanover Township supervisors to visit one of its operational data center facilities near Chicago in July. The trip occurred nearly two months after Prime submitted the project application to the township in May. Bryden said the trip was to give the officials an opportunity to see Prime’s Elk Grove Village data center campus, to see a working facility “in a mature data center market.” This area has over 20 operational data centers, so the supervisors could see “my product, and the product of my peers,” she said. It was intended to provide “educational context for what it is like in a data center, a modern operating data center.” Bryden said she did not recall whether the trip was initiated by a request from the supervisors or an offer from a Prime representative. Bryden served as the “tour guide” for this trip, she said, which included a paid lunch at a local pizza place. “It’s Chicago, so if you go and don’t get deep-dish what are you doing,” she said. The group from Hanover Township arrived early in the morning at a Chicago-area airport and left that same evening on July 2, she said. Bryden testified that she booked economy-class airline tickets for the group. She said she does not recall a full list of Hanover Township officials who attended the trip, but that Supervisor Chair Dale Handick and Vice Chair William Michael were there. According to Bryden, the group did not discuss the active permit application regarding the proposed Starpointe data center campus. The supervisors have been reviewing a conditional use permit application submitted by Prime in May for a large data center facility that would occupy around 120 acres of land in Starpointe Business Park. According to Pennsylvania State Ethics Commission Executive Director Mary Fox, elected officials in the commonwealth are legally allowed to accept certain gifts including airline tickets and meals, as long as any gifts worth over $600 are reported on annual Statement of Financial Interests disclosure forms. Handick did not comment on a range of questions regarding the trip.

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no EXCLUSIVO CNBC: Marvell projeta mais de US$ 30 bilhões em receita de data centers em 2028, diz CEO Publicado 07/10/2026 • 16:53 | Atualizado há 14 horas KEY POINTS A Marvell projeta uma forte expansão de seus negócios ligados à infraestrutura de inteligência artificial e data centers, com receita implícita superior a US$ 30 bilhões em 2028. Em entrevista exclusiva à CNBC, Matt Murphy, CEO da Marvell, afirmou que a estimativa representa uma forte revisão em relação à projeção de US$ 15 bilhões apresentada pela companhia dois anos atrás. “Dois anos atrás, estávamos em Nova York, no mesmo hotel, no mesmo local, falando sobre nosso crescimento em IA e data centers. E estávamos falando, naquela época, sobre US$ 15 bilhões de receita da Marvell para 2028”. Segundo Murphy, o consenso atual dos analistas já aponta para uma receita de data centers superior a US$ 30 bilhões em 2028. “Ela basicamente dobrou nesse período”, disse. O executivo afirmou que a companhia vem atualizando os investidores conforme o mercado de inteligência artificial evolui e que os resultados alcançados ao longo do caminho reforçaram a confiança nas projeções. A expansão também ocorre em um momento de aumento das expectativas para empresas de semicondutores ligadas à inteligência artificial. Murphy comentou a declaração feita por Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, que afirmou em junho que a Marvell poderia se tornar a próxima empresa de US$ 1 trilhão em valor de mercado. “Não foi ensaiado e foi chocante quando Jensen disse aquilo”, afirmou Murphy. Segundo ele, porém, uma avaliação desse tamanho não seria necessariamente incompatível com as perspectivas de receita da companhia nos próximos anos. Para o CEO da Marvell, uma das principais oportunidades está menos na capacidade de processamento individual dos chips e mais na infraestrutura necessária para conectar diferentes componentes dos sistemas de IA. Murphy explicou que o avanço da inteligência artificial inicialmente foi acompanhado por uma forte expansão da capacidade computacional, seguida por uma grande demanda por memória. O próximo gargalo, segundo ele, está na conectividade entre esses componentes. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC “Não há o suficiente na camada de conectividade para conectar todas essas coisas. Você tem muita computação instalada, muita memória instalada. Mas adivinha? Elas todas precisam conversar entre si através de interconexões ópticas de alta velocidade, redes de comutação”. O objetivo, segundo Murphy, é evitar que unidades de processamento ou memória permaneçam ociosas por falta de comunicação eficiente entre os componentes. A necessidade de conectividade também aumenta com a diversificação dos sistemas de IA. O executivo afirmou que aplicações de IA generativa, agentes e modelos de raciocínio estão ampliando a variedade de tipos de computação utilizados nos sistemas. “Quando você começa a falar sobre IA, agêntica e modelos de raciocínio, há cada vez mais tipos diversos de computação. Então, a camada de conectividade fica ainda mais complexa”. Murphy considera essa expansão o próximo grande desbloqueio do mercado de semicondutores. Segundo ele, o negócio da Marvell relacionado à conectividade acelerou desde que essa tese passou a ser apresentada aos investidores. O executivo também comentou a expansão do mercado de silício personalizado. Em abril de 2024, a companhia estimava um mercado total endereçável de US$ 40 bilhões para esse segmento. Agora, a projeção apresentada por Murphy é de US$ 235 bilhões até 2030. Segundo o CEO, a discussão sobre a viabilidade do mercado mudou significativamente nos últimos dois anos. “O debate era, na verdade, se o personalizado poderia sequer se materializar como uma fatia do mercado. Agora, você avança no tempo e não somos apenas nós. Todo esse segmento foi claramente consolidado como algo real”. A Marvell atua nesse mercado em diferentes áreas e estabeleceu uma meta de US$ 30 bilhões em receita com silício personalizado até 2030. A companhia espera alcançar mais de US$ 12 bilhões nesse negócio em 2028. Considerando a projeção de US$ 235 bilhões para o mercado até 2030, Murphy afirmou que a meta da Marvell representaria cerca de 13% de participação. “Nosso negócio em 2028 será de US$ 12 bilhões ou mais em personalizado. artigo.texto: A Plattsburgh man planned a data center in Chateaugay. Locals are pushing back The rumors started swirling a few months ago. Chateaugay, a small farming town in northern Franklin County, may soon get a data center. But little was known about the project, including who was behind it and what stage of development the data center was in. Chateaugay joins a growing list of towns across the country that developers are eyeing as demand for data processing sites grows amid the artificial intelligence boom. Last Monday evening, dozens of people showed up at the Chateaugay town board meeting looking for answers about the potential project. Turnout was so much higher than normal that the meeting was moved to a larger room. Paula King, who lives in Chateaugay, was among those who expressed some skepticism about the project. "I am all for local development, but I like to be sure that we’re mitigating any harm to the environment, to the people that live within the communities and that we maximize benefits from this," said King. Details of the proposed project The property where the potential data center would be built is a few miles south of downtown Chateaugay. The 19-acre property is the site of a former wood chip factory. In 2022, Joseph Church from Plattsburgh purchased the property for $500,000. Church is a veterinarian and a former partner at the Plattsburgh Animal Hospital, where he worked for more than two decades. According to his LinkedIn, Church is also the founder and CEO of New York GreenCloud, a company focused on "developing data center infrastructure powered by renewable energy.” A year after he bought the property, Church presented his data center proposal to the Chateaugay town board. According to his company's website, the data center could consume up to 15 megawatts of power, which is much smaller than the project currently under review in nearby Massena, which would be designed for 635 megawatts. Developer of the site in Chateaugay faces problems When it was first proposed, Chateaugay Town Supervisor Don Bilow said he was open to it. "When they presented the project, it looked like a nice project, but now we’re starting to get doubts about it," said Bilow after last week's meeting. Bilow said he hasn’t heard anything from Church in three years. Church also did not respond to multiple requests for comment for this article. Along with the site in Chateaugay, Church is also planning to build a data center at the Buena Vista biomass plant in Amador County, California. A local newspaper reporter from the Ledger Dispatch in northern California interviewed Church earlier this spring and asked about the project in Chateaugay. Despite it being listed as "in construction" on his company's website, Church admitted that the project has been stalled. "The problem with Chateaugay- it’s not abandoned due to any issues; it's that the site is not in the condition that Buena Vista was in," said Church. There was some work done on the site in Chateaugay a few years ago. Church hired an electrical company from Clinton County, but according to public court records, he never paid the company, so they sued. A judge ordered Church to pay back more than $38,000. In recent years, he has also been sued by two credit card companies over unpaid debt. In those two cases, Church was ordered to pay back a combined $54,000. Skepticism and fears arise over the proposed data center When he was interviewed earlier this spring, Church said he was still hopeful his business will take off, and he claimed that the community in Chateaugay was supportive of his project. "Chateaugay welcomes the restart of that place," said Church, later adding that "they would love to see it come back." But that’s not an accurate reflection of the local sentiment now that more people are aware of the project. According to some who were at Chateaugay’s town board meeting last week, most commenters were either skeptical of the data center or against it. "I fear that there’s too much unknown with what a data center is actually capable of," said Cecilia Merrill. Her top concern is about the environmental impact of a data center. Along with requiring a lot of power, data centers also need a lot of cooling capacity. The property Church owns is about 1,000 ft. from the Chateaugay River, where Merrill goes fishing about five times a week. "The brook trout in it are still thriving; they’re beautiful," said Merrill. "There’s wild fish in there, and there’s a color pink on some of them that I’ve never seen on any other spectrum of light.” She’s worried all that would be at risk if a data center was built near the river. Meanwhile, some others at the meeting said the area needs more industry. Griffon Wilde, who owns property in Ellenburg Center, said she is skeptical of the project, but she’s also sympathetic to the local economy. "There needs to be new industry coming here. There needs to be more opportunities for people to be something other than prison guards," said Wilde. "There’s got to be more coming in for this place to survive.” "It sounds like there's still time for Chateaugay to potentially stop something like this," added Wilde, "or at least make sure that it will be a positive and bring enough jobs to make it worth it." Drafting up a moratorium At its meeting last week, the Chateaugay town board heard about 30 minutes of public comment on the potential data center. In the end, the board agreed to work on a one-year moratorium that would ban any data centers from coming to town. There is currently a statewide moratorium in effect, but it only applies to projects larger than 50 megawatts, so it would not apply to the proposed project in Chateaugay. After a local moratorium expires, town supervisor Don Bilow said if a data center is officially proposed in the future, he’d treat it like any other development. "Any project, we always look at it and go from there. If it looks like it’s going to benefit the community, we definitely move forward

artigo.texto: NY hit pause on large data centers. A massive project in Massena may be exempt Over the past year, a proposed data center project has been the center of a tense community debate in Massena. New York Digital Investment Group (NYDIG) and its affiliate cryptocurrency operators, North Country Collocation Services (NCCS), want to build a 1.5 million-square-foot, 635-megawatt data center near the St. Lawrence River. That equals around 70% of the power produced at the huge Moses Saunders hydroelectric dam nearby. If approved, it would be one of the largest data centers in New York State. Close access to this hydropower has made Massena an ideal location for data center developers. This project is planned for the shuttered Alcoa East/Reynolds industrial site. The company's website says initial construction is slated for later this year. Earlier this year, Gov. Kathy Hochul signed an executive order temporarily restricting development of new hyperscale data centers exceeding 50 megawatts. These facilities used to power A.I. are controversial across the country. The moratorium gives state agencies more time to assess their impact. But the Massena project could be exempt from this statewide restriction. That’s because the moratorium isn’t a blanket ban on new data centers. It orders the DEC not to issue any new discretionary permits. But Massena officials say NCCS doesn’t require additional permits because it already applied for them back in 2020. Jason Pfotenhauer, director of St. Lawrence County's Planning Office, said that NCCS's exemption could be legitimate. "If they don’t need a state permit, then the moratorium wouldn’t be applicable," he said. "The applicant is saying, 'We don't need any official approval from the state because we're not going to meet any thresholds that would require us to get a state permit. So because of that, the moratorium doesn't apply to us.'" State officials haven't confirmed if NCCS is still subject to this moratorium. Massena opens the door Massena’s Town Board recently cleared a path for the data center by voting 3-2 against a local moratorium. Deputy supervisor Samuel Carbone and board members Adrian Taraska and Jared Hollander voted no. Hollander said the project is worth exploring. "Data centers, they are being built whether we have a say in it or not, not across the country alone but across the whole globe. So the opportunity that we have in front of us is control," he said. Supervisor Raymond Lancto and board member Kristy Baker voted in support of the data center restriction. Even if this project is exempt from the state moratorium, that does not mean it’s good to go. Hurdles remain, including those from the local government and the state. Massena’s Town Supervisor, Ray Lancto, said developers are just in the beginning phases. “There’s a review process," Lancto said. "It will have to go through the SEQRA process through the state and through DEC, and then it’ll have to gain all those approvals.” The DEC would evaluate the environmental, social, and economic impacts that data center construction and operation could have on the area. Data center controversy This data center has been controversial. Residents across the North Country are concerned it will drive up electricity bills, consume massive amounts of water, and cause noise and air pollution. NCCS says no local water will be used for cooling the data center because they're designing a fully sealed loop system. The St. Regis Mohawk Tribe issued a statement opposing all hyperscale data centers, saying they “pose known and unknown risks that could impact the health and well-being of our community.” "We met with Town of Massena representatives and sincerely hoped that the Town would not issue authorization for the continued growth of data centers in our area,” the Tribal Council said in a statement. Akwesasne has a long history of industry giants like Alcoa, General Motors, and Reynolds polluting the land and water around this data center site. Neddie Thompson has lived in Akwesasne her whole life. At a recent anti-data center protest in Massena, she said the town needs to take its time to learn more about this project so history isn’t repeated. "I grew up right on that river right next to that GM plant. We didn’t know nothing about what’s going on. We were little. And thyroids started first, then heart trouble, then our organs and our kidneys. We’ve got to get the facts on what this data center is, the noise pollution, the contamination of our water." Some people in Massena are supporting this data center because they hope it’ll provide jobs and boost an economy that’s struggled for decades. Mark Ryan was born and raised in Massena and was at a recent town board meeting. "When you look at this piece of paper and this information [on the developer's website], it talks about all the money they’re going to commit to invest in our community. If this is going to be good for our community. How could we turn it down? The community needs a lift," Ryan said. The company says the data center will provide 200 full-time jobs and an estimated 2,000 construction jobs. It's also pledging millions to support local schools, emergency services, roads, and other public services. Even if this data center project is exempt from a moratorium, Pfotenhauer from the county Planning Office said he doesn’t expect it to start anytime soon. "Projects don't happen overnight, right? Even if there were some requirements for the moratorium at the state level — this is not going to happen within a year. This project is not going to be built and developed in a year," Pfotenhauer said. During that time, he said there could be more regulation that comes out of the state moratorium. Massena's next town board meeting is Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, at 4:30 pm. It's not clear yet if the data center will be included in the day's discussions.

artigo.texto: BASF SE Leading integrated supplier for Li-ion batteries According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Solvents For Battery Electrolyte market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global market for solvents for battery electrolyte is entering a phase of structural expansion, underpinned by the rapid scaling of lithium-ion cell manufacturing and the accelerating transition to electric mobility. These high-purity organic solvents—primarily cyclic and linear carbonates, along with emerging fluorinated compounds—serve as the indispensable liquid medium enabling ion transport between electrodes. Unlike commodity industrial solvents, battery-grade electrolyte solvents must meet stringent purity thresholds, often at parts-per-million impurity levels, creating a distinct premium segment with high barriers to entry. Demand is overwhelmingly pull-through from electric vehicle gigafactory ramp-ups, making solvent consumption geographically tethered to cell manufacturing clusters in Asia-Pacific, North America, and Europe. As battery chemistries evolve toward high-nickel NMC, silicon anodes, and solid-state interfaces, solvent blend requirements are shifting, driving demand for fluorinated solvents and precise carbonate ratios. Supply remains constrained not by base chemical capacity but by specialized purification, fluorination, and moisture-control infrastructure. Qualification cycles with cell manufacturers are long, typically 12 to 24 months, rewarding incumbents with proven track records. This report provides a structured, commercially grounded analysis of the market from 2026 to 2035, covering demand architecture, supply chain dynamics, pricing logic, competitive structure, and regional outlooks. The baseline scenario for the global solvents for battery electrolyte market through 2035 anticipates robust volume growth, primarily driven by the expansion of lithium-ion battery production capacity to meet electric vehicle and stationary storage demand. The market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 12.5% from 2026 to 2035, reaching a market index of 325 (2025=100) by the end of the forecast period. This outlook assumes a steady increase in EV penetration rates, supportive government policies, and continued investment in gigafactory capacity, particularly in Asia-Pacific, North America, and Europe. The demand trajectory is not without volatility; it is closely tied to the scaling timelines of major OEMs and cell manufacturers, which can shift due to supply chain disruptions, raw material price fluctuations, or changes in subsidy regimes. However, the fundamental direction remains upward, supported by the irreplaceable role of high-purity solvents in battery performance and safety. Pricing is expected to remain multi-layered, with premiums for battery-grade certification, custom formulations, and moisture-free delivery. The competitive landscape will continue to bifurcate between integrated petrochemical majors and specialty pure-plays, with regional localization policies creating opportunities for niche purifiers. Key risks include potential delays in solid-state battery commercialization, which could alter solvent demand composition, and the impact of alternative battery chemistries such as sodium-ion, though these are not expected to significantly displace lithium-ion dominance within the forecast horizon. The electric vehicle sector is the primary engine of demand for battery electrolyte solvents, accounting for the majority of global consumption. As automakers ramp up production of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), gigafactories are being built at an unprecedented pace, particularly in China, the United States, and Europe. Each gigafactory requires a steady supply of high-purity solvents such as ethylene carbonate (EC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC) to produce electrolytes for lithium-ion cells. The demand is not merely volume-driven; it is increasingly quality-driven. EV batteries demand solvents with ultra-low moisture and impurity levels to ensure safety, cycle life, and fast-charging capability. Through 2035, as EV penetration increases and battery sizes grow, solvent demand will scale accordingly. Key demand-side indicators include EV sales volumes, gigafactory capacity announcements, and battery chemistry roadmaps. The shift toward high-nickel cathodes and silicon anodes will require solvent blends with higher fluorinated solvent content, creating new premium niches. Major cell manufacturers like CATL, LG Energy Solution, and Tesla are directly influencing solvent procurement strategies, often locking in multi-year supply agreements. Current trend: Dominant and rapidly growing. Major trends: Gigafactory capacity expansion in China, US, and Europe, Shift toward high-nickel NMC and silicon anode chemistries, Increasing demand for fluorinated solvents for high-voltage systems, and Localization of battery supply chains driven by policy incentives. Representative participants: CATL, LG Energy Solution, Tesla, BYD, and Panasonic. The stationary energy storage sector, encompassing grid-scale batteries, commercial and industrial (C&I) systems, and residential storage, is a growing demand driver for battery electrolyte solvents. As renewable energy penetration increases, the need for energy storage to balance supply and demand becomes critical. Lithium-ion batteries dominate this segment, though flow batteries and other technologies are emerging. Solvent demand from stationary storage is driven by the same purity requirements as EV batteries, but with different performance priorities: cycle life and cost per kilowatt-hour are often more important than energy density. artigo.texto: BYD Weighs Argentine Battery Plant as Brussels Moves to Seal Its Hybrid Loophole Published on 10/09/2026 at 07:41 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD is exploring a push into Argentina's lithium value chain, with battery cell manufacturing and energy storage systems at the centre of the plan. Executive Vice President Stella Li discussed the proposal with Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, though no investment figures or a shortlisted site emerged from the talks. For the Chinese automaker, the move would tie direct access to key battery raw materials to industrial processing on the ground. The South American overture lands alongside a solid early track record there. More than 10,000 vehicles have been sold in Argentina in the first year since the brand's official launch, supported by a distribution network of over 20 official outlets. Brussels Targets the Plug-In Hybrid Escape Route Far less welcoming is the reception taking shape in Europe. According to Bloomberg, the European Commission is preparing time-limited safeguard measures on hybrid vehicle imports from China, with a tariff quota model under discussion. Up to a set import volume, only the standard 10% duty would apply; shipments beyond that threshold would face a surcharge. Such restrictions would strike at a central pillar of BYD's European distribution strategy. Hybrids have served many Chinese manufacturers as an effective lever for softening European trade barriers: while BYD's pure electric cars have carried an additional EU tariff of 17% since October 2024, plug-in hybrids have been exempt from those special duties. Demand responded accordingly. Chinese vehicle imports in that segment climbed from 3,800 units in October 2024 to roughly 50,000 vehicles in July 2026. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? The Seal U DM-i has become the standout beneficiary, emerging as BYD's European workhorse. In Germany, the model recorded 11,291 new registrations between January and September 2026. UK brand sales, meanwhile, rose 80% year on year in September to 20,140 units, with the same vehicle driving growth. Diplomacy in Beijing, Factories in Europe The deliberations in Brussels coincide with a diplomatic push. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šef?ovi? is travelling to Beijing today for two days of talks, including negotiations with Chinese Trade Minister Wang Wentao over the bilateral trade deficit. Voluntary Chinese export restraints are viewed as unlikely, since Beijing rejects such quotas as a breach of World Trade Organization rules. To sidestep trade hurdles over the longer term, BYD is betting on regional production close to its sales markets. Plants are under construction in Hungary, Brazil and Thailand, and a possible takeover of an existing facility in southern Europe remains on the table, with talks under way over a Stellantis site. The approach also reflects broader global barriers: management has shelved entry into the US passenger car market for now, citing geopolitical risk. Li described geopolitical tensions as the single biggest obstacle to the group's worldwide expansion, pointing to a lack of stability and clarity in the United States as the reason for holding back. JPMorgan Downgrade Adds to the Pressure At home, the picture is mixed. BYD reported worldwide sales of 463,561 alternative-drive vehicles for September, yet volumes for January through September stood at just over 3.13 million units, 3.94% below the prior-year level. Analysts have taken note. Roughly a week ago, JPMorgan cut its rating on the stock from Overweight to Neutral and lowered its price target from HK$124 to HK$88, citing an expected industry slump in China, rising input costs and international trade barriers. Europe remains a priority regardless. On 12 October 2026, management plans a press conference and the unveiling of a new model at the Paris Motor Show. The market offered little relief. The shares closed Thursday's session down 1.3% at EUR 8.30, a decline of 22% since the start of the year. In today's trading the stock sits at EUR 8.33, barely above its 52-week low of EUR 8.03, weighed down by the looming Brussels restrictions and the heavy outlay on its own overseas cargo fleet — around USD 2.5 billion committed together with logistics partners — which is pressuring short-term earnings. artigo.texto: - Renewable - 1 min read AmpereHour Energy, Ampt partner to deploy direct-to-battery storage systems Partnership to target solar-plus-storage, data centres, EV charging, green hydrogen and battery augmentation projects AmpereHour Energy, a Pune-based full-stack battery energy storage system provider, on Thursday said it has partnered with US-based Ampt to distribute and service the latter’s DC power management products across India, South Asia, West Asia and Africa. According to the press release, this comes as the companies look to expand the deployment of direct-to-battery energy storage systems. “Firm, dispatchable renewable power is now the defining requirement of the energy transition. Our partnership helps hybrid projects capture more energy, lower capital costs and meet growing demand for clean, around-the-clock power,” said Aaron Gomolak, chief executive officer of Ampt, a DC optimiser company for large-scale systems. The partnership combines Ampt’s string optimisers and direct-to-battery (D2B) technology with AmpereHour’s battery energy storage systems (BESS), energy management software and project services to improve efficiency, reduce capital expenditure and enhance the reliability of renewable power projects. The companies said that they will target applications including utility-scale solar-plus-storage plants, data centres, EV charging infrastructure, solar repowering, co-located green hydrogen projects and battery capacity augmentation. Focus on cost and efficiency Ampt’s D2B architecture connects solar photovoltaic arrays directly to the battery’s DC bus, eliminating the need for a dedicated battery converter. The companies said this could lower overall system costs, improve round-trip energy efficiency and enhance long-term system performance. Ayush Misra, co-founder and chief executive of AmpereHour Energy, said that the collaboration would enable the company to offer cost-optimised solar-plus-storage solutions to project developers and utility customers. Pune-headquartered AmpereHour provides battery storage integration and energy management solutions across utility-scale, independent power producer and commercial and industrial segments.

artigo.texto: Inlyte Energy, a United States-based iron-sodium battery storage manufacturer, has announced a long-duration storage project with CutPeak Energy at Berkshire East Mountain Resort in Massachusetts. The project has been designed around the resort's energy profile, since its snowmaking pushes the electricity demand as high as 4 MW for a small part of the year. An iron-sodium battery of up to 80 MWh is therefore to be recharged during the long hours of low demand and to deliver power through the snowmaking peaks. During a grid outage, the same battery can be switched to the critical loads which keep the resort open as a shelter and a warming centre. The project is one of two demonstrations that the state has selected under its $40.3 million Advancing Massachusetts Power Energy Storage Grant Program. Under that award, the battery is to come online in 2028, and the project remains subject to final agreements, financing and approvals. Inlyte and CutPeak plan 80 MWh iron-sodium BESS at Berkshire East An iron-sodium battery of up to 80 MWh from Inlyte Energy is to carry the snowmaking peaks of a Massachusetts ski resort under a $40.3 million state grant program. artigo.texto: A BYD já definiu como pretende organizar suas marcas de luxo no Brasil. Em conversa com executivos da empresa durante o evento de apresentação da Denza, em Campos do Jordão (SP), o grupo confirmou, nesta terça-feira (6), que a Yangwang será sua marca topo de linha no País, posicionada acima da própria Denza. A estratégia terá, portanto, três níveis. A BYD continuará como marca principal do grupo, enquanto a Denza ocupará o espaço de premium de luxo e a Yangwang ficará no degrau mais alto, com a missão de disputar espaço com fabricantes de altíssimo luxo e desempenho. Segundo os executivos, a Yangwang terá como referências marcas como McLaren, Rolls-Royce e Aston Martin, além de fabricantes que também estudam avançar nesse segmento no Brasil, como a Cadillac. Durante a conversa, Marcelo Albino, Head de Produtos Denza e Desenvolvimento de Negócios na BYD Auto Brasil, classificou a Yangwang como aquilo que há de melhor atualmente em termos de automóveis produzidos na China. E já há um evento oficial de apresentação da nova divisão, que ocorrerá em Dubai (Emirados Árabes Unidos), no início de novembro. U7, U8 e U9 estão no radar A BYD ainda não definiu uma data para a chegada dos primeiros modelos da Yangwang ao mercado brasileiro. Existe, porém, um estudo de mercado em andamento e a expectativa é de que U7, U8 e U9 estejam entre os produtos avaliados para o País. Os três modelos representam diferentes propostas dentro da Yangwang. Resumidamente, o U7 é um sedã de luxo 100% elétrico; U8 será o SUV que atravessa alagamentos e rios; e o U9 é o cupê esportivo que atinge 490 km/h. A marca tem justamente a estratégia de atuar no segmento mais sofisticado do mercado, combinando alto desempenho, tecnologia e acabamento de extremo luxo, acima, por incrível que parece, de modelos como Porsche Panamera ou Taycan. Os executivos, no entanto, evitaram estabelecer um cronograma para a chegada dos carros. Portanto, a vinda dos modelos é tratada neste momento como uma possibilidade em estudo, e não como lançamento confirmado. Essa previsão só deve acontecer no evento de Dubai. Primeira loja deve ser em São Paulo Segundo Werner Schaal, Diretor Comercial da Denza Brasil, há interesse em expandir a rede tanto da Yangwang quanto da Denza. A expectativa é que a primeira concessionária da Yangwang no Brasil seja instalada em São Paulo, mas a BYD ainda não fechou todos os detalhes da operação. A intenção é ampliar posteriormente a presença da marca para outras regiões do País. Deve ser uma rede menor que a da Denza, portanto, não haverá uma replicação ou carros da Yangwang dentro de lojas da Denza, por exemplo. A tendência é que as duas marcas tenham concessionárias independentes, sem necessariamente dividir o mesmo endereço ou a mesma operação física. Apesar disso, o time que atualmente cuida da Denza dentro da estrutura da BYD também deverá assumir a operação da Yangwang no Brasil. Segundo os interlocutores ouvidos pelo Jornal do Carro, A estratégia indica que a BYD não pretende tratar suas marcas premium apenas como versões mais caras de seus carros convencionais. A ideia é criar uma estrutura própria para cada uma delas, com posicionamento e público diferentes. LEIA MAIS: - Aceleramos o YangWang U8, SUV da nova marca BYD no Brasil - BYD em Pequim: esportivo elétrico, SUVs de luxo e carro conceito que vira cinema - Após cancelamento, CFMoto anuncia nova data de lote de 700 motos Os executivos também destacaram a velocidade de evolução da indústria automobilística chinesa. A avaliação da BYD é que a transformação tecnológica do setor continuará acontecendo rapidamente e que fabricantes que demorarem a acompanhar esse movimento já estarão em desvantagem. A chegada da Yangwang representa justamente o passo seguinte dessa estratégia: depois de avançar sobre segmentos de volume com a BYD e entrar no mercado premium com a Denza, o grupo quer disputar também o espaço reservado às marcas de maior prestígio e preço. Ainda não há, desta forma, uma data definida para a estreia da Yangwang no Brasil. artigo.texto: KINGSTON, N.Y. — The city’s Common Council unanimously approved creating a task force to draft zoning regulations for utility-scale battery energy storage systems after proposals for such facilities caused controversy in neighboring communities. The Common Council approved the creation of the task force at its meeting on Tuesday, Oct. 6. After the proposal was modified by increasing the task force’s size to nine members, it was approved by an 8-0 vote. Teryl Mickens, D-Ward 5, was absent. Majority Leader Michele Hirsch said the city will commit to “full accountability,” with all task force meetings “strictly complying” with the state’s open meetings law. Hirsch said the task force will have a clearly defined six-month timeframe to do “comprehensive research,” collaborate with “stakeholders” and external experts on battery energy storage systems and draft new zoning regulations. This will allow the city to get ahead of any major project proposals with “thoughtful, legally sound zoning codes,” according to Hirsch. However, lawmakers have stated they are not certain if a lithium-ion battery energy storage facility could even be located in the city. When asked by a reporter in an email after September’s Laws and Rules Committee meeting, Common Council President Andrea Shaut said she does not believe there are any locations in the city where such a facility could be located. Such facilities consist of lithium-iron-phosphate battery cells packaged into modules, about the size of oversized briefcases, which are then put into racks and stored in containers resembling shipping containers. The facilities require proximity to a utility’s substation. The five proposals in Ulster County — three in the town of Ulster, one in Saugerties and one in New Paltz — are all proposed near a Central Hudson substation. Proposed lithium-ion battery energy storage projects, including the three projects proposed in the neighboring town of Ulster, have met with controversy across the county. Two of those projects, on Hurley Avenue in the town of Ulster, are close to the city line. Mission Clean Energy has proposed a 120-megawatt lithium-ion battery facility on a 7.3-acre site at 463-465 Hurley Ave. That project is about 500 feet west of the controversial Terra-Gen site at the former John A. Coleman Catholic High School, where the Town Board is being asked to approve a 250-megawatt lithium-ion facility on 15 acres. In the town of Ulster, board members are also reviewing a proposal from BayWa r.e. for a 150-megawatt lithium-ion battery facility on Frank Sottile Boulevard. It would be on about 10.4 acres adjacent to the former town landfill, with a new substation constructed on the other side of the road. It would be adjacent to a residential neighborhood and the 164-unit Ulster Gardens apartment complex. In the town of Saugerties, Key Capture Energy has proposed a 100-megawatt facility on Tomson’s Road near a Central Hudson substation that has met with opposition from residents and calls from Saugerties village officials for a moratorium on such projects. Hirsch’s pledge of strict compliance with the state’s Open Meetings Law comes after opponents of the Key Capture project in Saugerties accused a town zoning working group, whose meetings are not open to the public, of being out of compliance with the state law. Key Capture and Ulster County are also proposing a lithium-ion battery storage facility at the site of the county’s under-construction emergency communications center on Paradies Lane in the town of New Paltz.
