artigo.texto: Ataque ucraniano atinge centro de dados e afeta funcionamento da 'cortina de ferro digital' da Rússia Usuários relataram problemas sites de bancos, empresas de telecomunicações e serviços de e-mail; ação foi a primeira contra a infraestrutura digital russa desde 2022 Por O Globo e agências internacionais — Moscou Atualizado A Ucrânia realizou nesta quinta-feira um ousado ataque contra um centro de dados da gigante da internet russa, a Yandex, afetando o funcionamento de serviços e sites dentro do controlado ambiente digital da Federação Russa, também conhecido como RuNet ou “Cortina de Ferro Digital”. Foi a primeira ação militar ucraniana contra um centro de dados no país vizinho desde o início do conflito, em 2022, e pode marcar uma nova etapa na ofensiva contra alvos econômicos dos dois lados. - Incluindo cinco crianças: Escalada de ataques russos na Ucrânia deixa rastro de destruição e ao menos 63 mortos em dois dias - Quer ler mais notícias de Mundo? Acompanhe o canal no WhatsApp - Quer morar fora? Veja guia interativo do GLOBO que reúne informações sobre 36 países De acordo com a Yandex, os drones caíram no centro de dados de Sasovo, a pouco mais de 200 km de Moscou, provocando um incêndio e interrompendo as operações. O local também abriga dois supercomputadores da empresa empregados no treinamento de redes neurais. A extensão dos danos não foi revelada, mas a companhia — cujas ações despencaram na bolsa de Moscou — garantiu que estava lidando com as consequências, restaurando serviços e que os principais serviços ao público não foram afetados. "A extensão dos danos à infraestrutura ainda está sendo avaliada. Ainda não podemos confirmar a possibilidade de restaurar os equipamentos do data center em Sasovo", afirmou a empresa, citada pela agência de notícias estatal RIA. Contudo, consumidores relataram dificuldades no acesso aos serviços de e-mail e armazenamento em nuvem da Yandex. Portais de bancos, empresas de telecomunicações e até de venda de passagens da estatal ferroviária apresentaram instabilidade ao longo do dia, assim como ao menos uma empresa de ônibus de Moscou. Ao mesmo tempo, não houve problemas em aplicativos de transporte como o Yandex Taxi. O ataque foi o primeiro registrado contra centros de dados russos desde o início da guerra, e embora seus efeitos tenham sido amenizados, ele demonstra certa vulnerabilidade digital da Rússia e sua controlada internet interna, a RuNet, apelidada também de “Cortina de Ferro Digital”, uma referência modernizada aos tempos da Guerra Fria. Com base em uma lei de 2019, o governo determinou que os operadores instalassem equipamentos que permitissem ao Estado identificar, filtrar e até bloquear conteúdos, e até, em último caso, bloquear o acesso da rede à internet externa. Posteriormente, o Roskomnadzor, o órgão de controle de conteúdo russo, passou a bloquear serviços, portais e aplicativos, ameaçando com processos aqueles que usassem VPNs, as redes privadas virtuais, para burlar a censura. Foram os sites localizados dentro desse ecossistema digital nacional que se viram afetados nesta quinta-feira. A ação ucraniana parece ter sido uma resposta a recentes bombardeios russos contra centros de dados no país, que afetaram serviços digitais ao redor do país — de redes de telefonia a operações bancárias e derrubaram redes de TV e serviços de streaming. Especialistas dizem que, ao contrário da Rússia, a ampla oferta local de acesso à internet impede um apagão completo, mesmo sob bombas. “A internet desaparecerá na Ucrânia? Claro que não. A infraestrutura será reestruturada e locais alternativos serão estabelecidos”, disse Oleksandr Fediienko, membro da Comissão Parlamentar de Segurança Nacional, Defesa e Inteligência, em publicação no Facebook. Os ataques se inserem em um componente econômico da guerra iniciada em 2022, que teve nos bombardeios contra os armazéns da gigante russa do comércio eletrônico Wildberries um marco. Cerca de 20 instalações da empresa, apelidada de “Amazon da Rússia”, foram afetadas, provocando perdas estimadas em mais de US$ 8 bilhões.

artigo.texto: A new University of Maryland Baltimore County poll shows widespread concern among Maryland likely voters about data centers, with 80% saying they believe the facilities will have a mostly negative impact on household electricity costs Just 6% of those surveyed said new data centers would have a mostly positive impact on electric costs. Seventy-five percent expect a negative impact on the quality of life for people living near data center sites. Opposition extends to whether new data centers should be built at all. Among 370 likely voters asked about new data centers being built in Maryland, 78% opposed them and 13% supported them. A separate group of 406 voters was asked about a new data center being built near their community, with 77% opposed and 16% in support. Voters also expressed concerns about the environmental impact. Sixty-eight percent said new data centers would have a mostly negative impact on water quality, while 60% said the same about air quality. The potential economic benefits didn't fare much better. Forty-nine percent said data centers would have a mostly negative impact on Maryland's economy, compared with 19% who expect a positive impact. Forty-eight percent expect a negative impact on state and local tax revenue, while 20% expect a positive one. When it comes to jobs and employment opportunities, 37% expect a negative impact, 28% expect no real impact and 26% expect a positive impact. Data centers weren't the only issue that likely voters expressed concerns about. The poll also found negative views of Maryland's economy and the direction of the state, while Gov. Wes Moore's job approval remained slightly higher than his disapproval. Nearly half of likely voters, 49%, said Maryland is on the wrong track, compared with 37% who believe the state is headed in the right direction. Views on the state's direction varied sharply by party. Half of Democrats said Maryland is headed in the right direction, while 30% said it's on the wrong track. Among Republicans, 90% said the state is on the wrong track, and 7% said it's headed in the right direction. Fifty-five percent of unaffiliated voters said Maryland is on the wrong track. The poll found 49% of likely voters approve of the job Wes Moore is doing as governor, while 42% disapprove and 8% said they don't know. Among Democrats, 70% approve of Wes Moore's job performance. Among Republicans, 7% approve and 88% disapprove. Unaffiliated voters were more likely to disapprove, 49% to 37%. The poll also found broad dissatisfaction with Maryland's economy. Eighty-one percent of likely voters rated economic conditions in the state over the past year as poor or fair. Just 17% described conditions as good or excellent. Looking ahead, 43% expect economic conditions to be worse a year from now, 37% think they'll be about the same and 12% expect them to improve. When asked what they consider when evaluating the state's economy, 94% pointed to the prices of everyday goods and services. Personal finances followed at 90%, housing costs at 86%, state taxes and fees at 84%, interest rates at 74%, unemployment and job reports at 67% and the stock market at 41%. Respondents could select more than one answer. Artificial intelligence also received largely negative marks. Sixty-seven percent of likely voters said they believe AI will have a negative impact on society, compared with 23% who expect a positive impact. Negative views crossed party lines, with 71% of Democrats, 57% of Republicans and 70% of unaffiliated voters saying they expect AI to have a negative impact on society. The UMBC Poll surveyed 776 Maryland likely voters from Sept. 22 through Sept. 27 using live telephone interviews and text-to-web surveys. The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.5 percentage points. UMBC classified registered voters as likely voters if they said they were either "absolutely certain" or "very likely" to vote in the November 2026 general election. The results were weighted by gender, age, race, geography, and educational attainment This is a developing story, so check back with WMAR2News.com for updates. artigo.texto: O grupo francês de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial Sesterce anunciou planos para desenvolver um complexo de data centers em Jämsä, na região central da Finlândia, com investimento superior a €10 bilhões, equivalente a US$ 11,21 bilhões. Segundo a empresa, a primeira etapa terá capacidade de 200 megawatts e obras previstas para começar em 2026. O empreendimento ocupará as instalações de uma antiga fábrica de papel, fechada em 2021, e já conta com um cliente-âncora. No longo prazo, a Sesterce pretende superar 1 gigawatt de capacidade de IA no país, utilizando áreas industriais existentes. A expansão, porém, será condicionada à demanda do mercado, e não foram informados prazo de conclusão, identidade do cliente ou estrutura de financiamento. Principais fatos e números - O investimento planejado supera €10 bilhões, ou US$ 11,21 bilhões. - A primeira fase terá capacidade de 200 MW. - As obras iniciais estão previstas para começar em 2026. - O projeto ficará em Jämsä, na região central da Finlândia. - O local abrigava uma fábrica de papel fechada em 2021. - A Sesterce afirma já ter um cliente-âncora para o complexo de data centers de IA. Por que isso importa para empresários e investidores O plano pode ampliar a oferta europeia de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial e criar oportunidades para fornecedores de energia, construção, equipamentos, conectividade e serviços de data center. A reutilização de uma área industrial também indica potencial para reconversão de ativos desativados. Para investidores e empresas dependentes de computação intensiva, a capacidade prevista pode representar uma nova alternativa regional. Contudo, o investimento ainda é um plano: a expansão acima de 1 GW dependerá da demanda, enquanto cronograma integral, financiamento, custos de energia e identidade do cliente-âncora não foram divulgados.

artigo.texto: WEST JORDAN, Utah — As Utah prepares for additional data center projects, questions remain about how those facilities affect nearby neighborhoods. To better understand those impacts, FOX 13 News visited a West Jordan neighborhood near the Novva data center, where residents have lived alongside the facility for several years. Lairn Finlayson has lived in the neighborhood for about a decade. He said the area has changed significantly over the years. Before the data center was built, Finlayson said the land nearby was open space where residents could occasionally see wildlife. “We used to watch the antelope out in the field and deer once in a while,” Finlayson said. Today, that field is home to the Novva data center, located several hundred feet from his home. Despite the change, Finlayson said the facility itself has not been a major concern. “It doesn't bother. I'm retired, so it doesn't bother me that bad,” Finlayson said. Here are the ties between the Stratos data center and the U.S. military: Finlayson said other development has had a more noticeable effect on the neighborhood. He pointed to a nearby apartment complex under construction west of the area. “I went to Bingham High School up in Copperton and used to be able to look out my front door and see the B on the hill and remind me of the old days. But, can't see that anymore. You see apartments,” Finlayson said. Another resident, Mohsin, lives across the road from the data center’s entrance. He invited FOX 13 News into his backyard to demonstrate what he described as minimal noise coming from the facility. “Once in a while you hear this sound," Mohsin said. He said neither the noise nor the workers commuting to the site have created problems for his family. “There are a lot of people working. But they don't bother you. They don't honk, they mind their own business. They go in, in and out,” Mohsin said. Not all residents shared that view. Two people living on the same street, roughly a football field away from the data center, said they were bothered by noise. However, both declined requests to speak on camera. FOX 13 News requested records from the West Jordan Police Department for noise complaints in the surrounding area during the past year. The search returned three police reports: one involving loud music and two involving a rooster. None were related to the data center. Ryan Stock, who also lives nearby, said he has not experienced any issues. “They're great neighbors. We've never had any problems. No noise,” Stock said. FOX 13 News also asked West Jordan officials how they balance growth with quality of life concerns. Paul Jerome, the city's assistant administrator, said the city has not received complaints about the Novva data center but takes resident concerns seriously. “Our mission as a city is the health, welfare, and safety of our residents. Tax revenue is great. We also want to make sure that the residents who live here enjoy living here,” Jerome said. He was not surprised tp learn that many residents interviewed spoke positively about the facility. “The data center itself actually was the one that did a lot of the outreach for the residents, you know, communicating what they were going to be doing, what it was going to look like, as well as continued outreach to this day,” Jerome said. He added that data centers contribute to the city's tax base. “If businesses weren't offsetting some of that tax base, that gets put put onto the residents' backs to have the same kind of services. So they do they do a lot for a city from a tax base perspective,” Jerome said. The Novva data center occupies about 100 acres. While considerably smaller than the proposed Stratos project in Box Elder County, which is planned for a 20,000-acre site, it is similar in scale to the proposed Volition data center in Spanish Fork, which is planned to occupy about 1 million square feet. As those and other projects move through the planning process, residents in affected communities continue asking many of the same questions West Jordan residents faced years ago. Stock recalled meeting a man from Eagle Mountain who stopped by the neighborhood to ask about living near a data center. “We were all just hanging out, and a guy stopped by, and he said he was from Eagle Mountain, and he had concerns about the data center being built by him. And so we were able to tell him the same thing. Just they're good neighbors. We haven't had any problems with them at all. Quiet, not nothing. Yeah. So. We thought that was interesting that he would stop, take his time to drive around and ask questions to other people,” Stock said. For some longtime residents, the conversation is about more than data centers. Growth continues across Utah, changing communities that have looked the same for decades. “It was just this little neighborhood with a couple houses in it,” Stock said. Finlayson said the changes can be difficult to watch, but he sees them as part of life. “You get old, you get sad because when you see all this construction going on, but that's life,” Finlayson said. artigo.texto: During the National Day holiday, the energy storage market maintained its pre-holiday operating pace, with no clear signs of weakening on the demand side. Project construction and grid connections continued to advance in China, while markets outside China extended from order signing toward financing, construction, and commercial operations. Entering Q4, the industry's focus is shifting. Compared with the earlier emphasis on order volume and production schedule growth, whether projects can be delivered, connected to the grid, and converted into actual installations on schedule will become a more important basis for judging the sustainability of demand. In China, energy storage projects in Xinjiang, Shanghai, and other regions completed grid connections one after another, and some projects in south China also continued to advance. The earlier project pipeline is gradually being converted into installations. However, there are still notable differences in project progress across regions. Some projects in Inner Mongolia and other areas are affected by factors such as transmission works and grid connection conditions, leaving a certain time lag between equipment delivery and actual grid connection. For projects that have already completed procurement and equipment delivery, grid connection delays reflect a postponement of demand realization rather than weaker demand for battery cells. In Q4, the Chinese market needs to focus on the grid connection conversion efficiency of earlier concentrated construction projects to assess whether the release of installations can accelerate further. Outside China, demand support is extending from order signing toward financing and commercial operations. Some energy storage projects in markets such as the UK and the US continue to secure long-term revenue arrangements and financing, while new projects in India have also entered the commercial operation stage. The certainty of project implementation outside China is still strengthening. As project revenue models become clearer and financing conditions improve, this will continue to support subsequent equipment procurement and project construction. However, energy storage projects outside China generally have long cycles from signing to equipment delivery and then to grid connection and operation, with clear cross-year execution characteristics. Therefore, when assessing short-term demand, it is still necessary to distinguish between order volume and the actual pace of delivery. Supply side, production schedule expectations before the holiday remained on a growth trajectory. Battery cell supply is expected to continue increasing in Q4, but the release of growth is still affected by the production ramp-up progress of large-capacity cells and the supply of some upstream materials. Currently, capacity utilization rates at top-tier players stay high, and with downstream order support, the industry's production schedule still has a foundation for continued growth. At the same time, long duration energy storage (LDES) projects continue to advance, further broadening energy storage application scenarios, but their impact on the short-term battery cell demand structure will still be released mainly in a gradual manner. Overall, the energy storage market did not cool significantly during the National Day holiday, and earlier orders still provide strong support for Q4 demand. Going forward, the industry's focus will shift further from "order growth" to "order fulfillment." In China, the key observation will be the release of projects pending grid connection, while outside China, the focus will be on order delivery and project execution efficiency. Battery cell shipments and ESS installations are expected to maintain growth in Q4, but the mismatch in their pace will persist. As previously delivered projects are gradually connected to the grid, the speed at which installations catch up with battery cell shipments will become an important observation point for Q4. artigo.texto: During the floods of 2023 and 2024, Vermonters saw neighbors come together to support one another through difficult times, creating connection, resilience, possibility and joy in their communities. It’s those qualities that moved filmmaker Bess O’Brien to create her new documentary, “Every Day: Big and Small.” Currently on tour around the state, the Rutland Free Library will host a screening of the film Saturday at 7 p.m. “I felt like people are supporting each other and doing things for their neighbors and communities, creating hope and inspiration every day; we just don’t talk about it,” O’Brien said. Aiming away from a deep dive on one story, O’Brien started looking for people who were doing impactful things in their small towns and cities across the state, and gathered those stories together. “I wanted to explore what’s working in Vermont, but I wanted to do more of a poetic type film with a series of stories, and that’s how it started,” O’Brien said. Told in a series of vignettes, the film highlights various individuals around the state, including people who are in recovery, men who are coming out of domestic violence situations, and teenagers who are doing positive things for their communities. Starting with her hometown of Peacham, O’Brien hit the ground running with a story of a family impacted by flooding. Her film then led her to St. Johnsbury and beyond as she followed the leads from locals she met along the way. O’Brien said she heard about the “Fierce Friday” drag show at the Rutland Elks Club from somebody she knew who had been to it. “I thought, ‘Wow, that is just so cool, I’ve got to shoot that,’” O’Brien said. Kamryn Eatherton, a local drag queen who performs as Bethadone Clinique, said O’Brien and her team were kind and supportive of what they were doing. Eatherton noted it can be scary— especially in a small town — to invite someone into your space when you know your space isn’t always welcomed by the general public. “It was just a dream come true to be able to be a part of such a cool project and to showcase a little bit of what the LGBTQ community has to offer, especially in Rutland and central Vermont,” Eatherton said. O’Brien said she enjoyed shooting the drag show and loved the fact that two very different cultures were working together, enjoying each other and having fun. “I think in our way of thinking about these two different entities, we wouldn’t necessarily think that they would work well together, but they did, and everyone enjoyed themselves, and everyone was so complimentary of each other,” she said. “That was a wonderful way of talking about how our differences don’t matter, and that’s a high point in the film.” Kelley Mills, an agriculture teacher at Patricia A. Hannaford Center in Middlebury who works with young, aspiring farm girls, said O’Brien has a special way of connecting with people on every level, explaining the intentionality she has when creating a story. Mills teaches teens pursuing a broad spectrum of agriculture careers. She explained how development during the teen years can be tumultuous, and many find it difficult to identify and connect with others who share the same interests and passions. However, she said her classroom provides a “safe haven” for students to connect with people who share an interest in agriculture. “(Bess) and Patrick Kennedy, the individual behind the camera, immediately set us at ease, which allowed the magic of my students and their stories to shine through,” Mills said. “I get to see this every day, but to share the pure joy of these students with others through this film is pure magic.” Explaining the importance she thinks the message of the film holds in our world right now, O’Brien said, “I think our country is very divided and there’s a lot of sense of doom and gloom. People are not feeling very hopeful for the future, so I hope that this movie gives people a sense that there is a possibility for good things, and that we can change things around them.” Eatherton said that after the audience watches his section he hopes they know they are 100% welcome in his corner and at his table, no questions asked. “I don’t think that drag shows are only for the LGBTQ, but for everyone to have fun and enjoy,” Eatherton said. “Small communities that get together to put on events or programming really pack a punch and make a difference in a community.” Eatherton said O’Brien didn’t just make their community feel like they were one small little snippet; rather, they felt like we were the whole documentary. O’Brien, said the film’s title — “Every Day: Big and Small” — refers to everyday moments of connection and resilience. She said a small moment can mean a big thing for somebody, and that kind of interconnection happens all the time here in Vermont. “Sometimes we only think that big things are happening in the cities and more urban areas but actually in small little communities, people are making huge differences, and I just want people to recognize how unique and connected Vermont is,” she said. Tickets for the screening are $15, and can be bought in advance at www.catamountarts.org or at the door. news @rutlandherald.com

artigo.texto: Key Capture Energy NY1 at Luther Forest in Stillwater was the first utility-scale battery energy storage system in New York. Ground was broken at the facility in 2018. AMSTERDAM — Amsterdam is following through on plans to ban battery energy storage systems in the city, citing public safety concerns. The Common Council has introduced a law that would modify city code to prohibit battery energy storage systems in all zoning districts within the city, as well as a separate law to end an ongoing moratorium on battery and utility-scale solar systems. Public hearings on each law will be held Oct. 20 starting at 5:40 p.m. during the council’s committee of the whole meeting before its regular meeting at 6 p.m. The battery ban was recommended by an ad hoc committee of city officials and employees that studied the potential benefits and dangers of the systems. The committee concluded the systems pose serious fire and public safety concerns and there isn’t a way to separate them from densely populated areas of the city. “I think they're being cautious and I think cautious is the proper approach,” Mayor Michael Cinquanti said Wednesday. Safety concerns have surged following fires at lithium-ion battery facilities in Jefferson, Orange and Suffolk counties in summer 2023. Fire broke out at a facility in Warwick in Orange County for a second time in December 2025. The state has since updated its fire code to introduce stricter safety standards for the systems that took effect this year. The city is poised to become the latest among a growing number of communities to ban the controversial systems, including the towns of Amsterdam, Florida and Glen in Montgomery County. The town of Mohawk has a moratorium in place as potential zoning updates are considered. In Fulton County, the towns of Johnstown, Northampton and Perth have either enacted or extended battery moratoriums this year, as did the city of Johnstown while Gloversville banned the systems outright. “There is no safe place within city limits that if something were to happen, that it wouldn't pose a danger,” Amsterdam Ward 4 Alderman Christopher Carpenter said previously. Amsterdam enacted a six-month moratorium on industrial solar and battery systems last year to give officials time to study the technology and develop potential updates to city code to regulate them amid development pressure. The moratorium was extended this spring to Jan. 5. Officials realized city code didn’t address standalone battery systems when Carson Power presented conceptual plans to the Planning Commission last year seeking feedback on a 5 megawatt system tentatively planned at 43 Verbarska Ave. The company informed officials in May it was instead considering a 12.5 megawatt project at an unspecified site on Edson Street. Corporation Counsel Anthony Casale said the proposed local laws would affirmatively prohibit battery energy storage systems throughout the city while restoring the solar regulations the city already had in place. Amsterdam’s moratorium included utility-scale solar due to the overlap between the systems in city code, but no changes to the solar regulations are planned. Although he understands the fears surrounding battery systems, Cinquanti hopes the technology will improve over time and overcome the safety concerns to support green energy initiatives. “Clean energy is a big challenge for our country and so I'm hoping that all these technologies that advance clean energy advance in terms of their ability to provide that energy … in a way in which everyone can be confident that they are good investments,” Cinquanti said. “I don't think BESS is there yet.”

artigo.texto: XBM USA and SiCAM Technologies Collaborate to Advance Next-Generation Silicon-Sulfur Battery Technology Collaboration pairs SiCAM's low-cost silicon-carbon anode material with XBM's sulfur cathode and cell technologies, to offer US battery OEMs an integrated silicon-sulfur (Si-S) battery platform. LOS ANGELES, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- XBM USA LLC ("XBM") and SiCAM Technologies, Inc. ("SiCAM") today announced a technology collaboration to develop a Silicon-Sulfur (Si-S) very high-energy-density battery materials platform by coupling SiCAM's silicon-carbon (Si-C) anode material with XBM's lithium-sulfur (Li-S) cathode materials and advanced cell technologies. Silicon-sulfur is amongst one of the most promising next-generation battery cathode and anode chemistry platforms, with substantially higher theoretical energy density than conventional li-ion batteries (LIBs). Silicon is the second-most-abundant element in the Earth's crust, sulfur is a U.S. petroleum-refining byproduct, and XBM's Li-S cathode is derived from lignin, an abundant U.S. paper pulping byproduct. Asia, predominantly China, currently controls ~80–95% of the global battery cell and materials supply chain. U.S. battery manufacturers are seeking better, lower-cost, domestically sourced chemistries that reduce reliance on foreign materials. This shift creates opportunities for U.S. OEMs to leapfrog legacy technologies. Jon Shan, Chief Technology Officer of XBM USA, said, "Our near-term objective is to optimize our high-capacity Li-S cathode and SiCAM's Si-C anode in a first-of-its-kind silicon-sulfur battery platform, initially targeting high-energy-density, lightweight eMobility battery applications such as eVTOLs and drones." SiCAM's proprietary silicon anode material and process are unique amongst all other Si-C anode products made today. Most other Si-C anode material developers use silane (silicon) in a CVD process to make their Si-C anode products. SiCAM uses chlorosilane (TCS) silicon in a fluidized-bed chemical vapor deposition (FB-CVD) process. This novel approach creates a true bonded silicon-composite primary structure, helping to reduce the 300% silicon swelling problems experienced during battery charge and discharge cycles. On the cathode side, XBM's high-capacity Li-sulfur cathode targets improved sulfur utilization, cycle life and cell-level energy density using abundant industrial byproducts, such as sulfur and lignin. "This silicon-sulfur cell technology collaboration is the natural evolution of our company's US centric "Sustainable Battery" vision avoiding longstanding battery chemistries that are mined, more expensive, and foreign sourced and controlled" said Phillip Roberts, co-founder of SiCAM Technologies and XBM USA. About XBM USA LLC XBM is a US sustainable high-capacity battery cathode, anode and advanced cell development company. Its flagship product is a high-capacity Li-S (Li-S) sulfur cathode active material (CAM) and new biomass-based carbon anode materials. The XBM Li-S technology is based on its proprietary CarbonX porous carbon sol-gel process, made with lignin-based byproduct materials and infused high-sulfur loadings and catalysts. About SiCAM Technologies, Inc. SiCAM Technologies, Inc. is the exclusive licensee of the patented, high-capacity Silicon-carbon (Si-C) Composite Anode Material named SiCAM™. The company is in the process of commercializing its low-cost Si-C anode material and is currently working on establishing SiCAM™ Si-C anode material production operations in the US. Media Contact Neil Martin | XBM USA LLC 707-953-0522 [email protected] www.xbmusa.com SOURCE Xponential Battery Materials (XBM USA LLC)

artigo.texto: On October 2, South Korean research firm SNE Research released its latest installation data. From January to August 2026, global power battery installations totaled 844.2 GWh, up 19.7% YoY. In August alone, installations reached 116.8 GWh, up 14.3% YoY, slower than July's 23.3% growth. Among the top 10 companies, seven Chinese firms held a combined 73.3% market share, up 3.6 percentage points YoY. What is evident is that the global power battery market continues to expand, with Chinese battery producers steadily growing their market share and further consolidating their leading positions. Meanwhile, the combined market share of Japanese and South Korean companies continues to be squeezed, with competitive dominance increasingly concentrated in the Chinese camp. In terms of YoY changes in installations, from January to August 2026, among the global top 10 power battery installation companies, only SK On posted a YoY decline, down 14.5%. The remaining nine companies all achieved YoY growth, with REPT Battero newly entering the list at a growth rate of 126.3%, and EVE growing over 50%. In terms of market share, compared with the same period in 2025, among the global top 10 power battery installation companies from January to August 2026, CATL, CALB, Gotion High-tech, EVE, SVOLT, and REPT Battero achieved positive YoY growth, while BYD, LGES, Panasonic, and SK On saw declines of varying degrees. In terms of ranking changes, compared with the same period last year, the top 10 installation rankings from January to August 2026 underwent a significant reshuffle: the top four remained unchanged—CATL, BYD, LGES, and CALB. Gotion High-tech moved up sharply from 7th place last year to 5th, displacing SK On, which fell to 8th. Panasonic held steady at 6th. EVE climbed two spots to 7th. SVOLT rose one spot from 10th to 9th. In addition, compared with the same period last year, REPT Battero newly entered the list at 10th place, with installations 1 GWh ahead of 11th-place Sunwoda. Samsung SDI, previously ranked 8th, dropped out of the top 10. On a MoM basis, compared with January-July 2026, battery company rankings remained unchanged. In terms of the competitive landscape, from January to August, the combined share of CATL, BYD, CALB, Gotion High-tech, EVE, SVOLT, and REPT Battero rose from 72.8% in January-July to approximately 73.3%, up 3.6 percentage points YoY. Among them, CATL and BYD together held 54.5% of the market, with Chinese companies performing strongly overall. Specifically, CATL's market share reached 39.4%, up 1.7 percentage points YoY, maintaining its global No. 1 position with 333 GWh of installations, up 25.2% YoY. BYD's market share slipped to 15.1%, but it remained firmly in second place with installations of 127.9 GWh, up 6.2% YoY. CALB ranked fourth with 44.4 GWh of installations, up 32.6% YoY, holding a 5.3% market share. Gotion High-tech ranked fifth with 41.5 GWh of installations, up 47.1% YoY, holding a 4.9% market share. EVE ranked seventh with 29.5 GWh of installations, up 53.9% YoY, holding a 3.5% market share. SVOLT ranked ninth with 22 GWh of installations, up 39.3% YoY, holding a 2.6% market share. REPT Battero ranked tenth with 20.3 GWh of installations, up 126.3% YoY, holding a 2.4% market share. SNE noted that the continued rise in Chinese battery companies' market share is attributable to leveraging their domestic client base and LFP-driven cost competitiveness to expand sales, while also extending supply arrangements to overseas OEMs and the commercial vehicle segment. Among them, BYD's installations grew only 6.2% YoY, mainly because its EV deliveries in China fell 33.6%. By contrast, its usage in markets outside China grew 66.5% from 23.8 GWh to 39.7 GWh, with overseas sales in August setting a new monthly record. As BYD expands its sales network and local production in Europe, Southeast Asia, and South America, the impact of the domestic market slowdown is expected to ease as its overseas market share rises. In stark contrast to the strong momentum of Chinese companies, Japanese and South Korean battery makers have seen their growth pace slow noticeably, with cracks appearing in their camp's structure. After Samsung SDI dropped out of the top 10, LGES and SK On together recorded installations of 93.2 GWh, with their combined global market share shrinking from 13.7% in the same period last year to 11%. Among them, LGES ranked third with 68.3 GWh, but its 0.9% growth rate lagged the broader market. SK On, affected by the electrification pace adjustments of its North American and European clients, recorded installations of only 24.9 GWh, down 14.5% YoY, with its market share falling to 2.9%. Japan's Panasonic maintained 6th place with 29.7 GWh of installations, up a slight 1.8% YoY. The rebound in installations came from Tesla's sales growth in North America, but the company's growth rate also trailed the average, with its market share declining from 4.1% to 3.5%. SNE noted that from January to August 2026, the global power battery market grew 20% YoY, but regional divergence intensified. In China, a 2% consumption tax on domestically sold lithium-ion batteries took effect in September, and the battery export VAT rebate is planned to be canceled in January next year. As a result, Chinese battery suppliers' pricing policies and the pace of their overseas production are likely to affect competition at year-end. According to data released by the China Automotive Power Battery Industry Innovation Alliance, from January to August, China's cumulative power battery installations reached 489.1 GWh, up 17.0% YoY. Compared with the same period in 2025, from January to August this year, CATL, REPT Battero, EVE, Gotion High-tech, LG Energy Solution, Jiyao Tongxing, Zenergy, Greater Bay Technology, Inpai Battery, and CORNEX New Energy achieved improvements of varying degrees. Among them, CATL posted the largest gain at 1.99 percentage points.

artigo.texto: Finlândia freia construção de dois 'data centers' da Google por impacto ambiental Empresa responsável por obras não teria apresentado reltório de avaliação; agência do governo investiga corte de mais de 300 hectares de floresta Uma agência governamental finlandesa ordenou, nesta terça-feira (6), que a Google suspenda a construção de novos "data centers" em dois municípios da Finlândia no mais tardar em 23 de outubro de 2026, à espera de uma avaliação de seu impacto ambiental. - Impactos visíveis: Chegada de 'datar centers' da Google muda vida na zona rural da Finlândia - Onde está Samba? Capivara ‘fugitiva’ vira celebridade após passar mais de seis meses desaparecida na Inglaterra Estes projetos fazem parte de um investimento de 13 bilhões de euros (R$ 72,7 bilhões) anunciado na Finlândia, o maior investimento da gigante tecnológica americana na Europa no âmbito da inteligência artificial. Durante uma visita na semana passada à cidade de Muhos, uma jornalista da AFP observou o ir e vir de retroescavadeiras. Em frente à fazenda de um dos moradores com quem conversou, a floresta tinha desaparecido de um terreno adquirido pela Google. - Caribe em Ipanema: Descoberta de bancos de algas calcárias cor-de-rosa surpreende pesquisadores; veja - Quer morar fora? Guia reúne informações sobre 36 países A agência finlandesa de supervisão exigiu, em um comunicado, que sejam suspensas "todas as medidas preparatórias suscetíveis de modificar de forma significativa o meio ambiente no âmbito dos projetos de 'data centers' previstos em Muhos e Kajaani", no noroeste do país. A agência abriu uma investigação pela suspeita de que a empresa Tuike Finland, que representa a Google, cortou mais de 300 hectares de floresta em Muhos sem realizar previamente a avaliação de impacto ambiental. As obras devem ser interrompidas até que seja feita esta avaliação, detalhou a agência. "Entendemos as preocupações expressas e reconhecemos que, neste caso concreto, não estivemos à altura de nossos próprios padrões, que são elevados", admitiu Sondre Ronander, porta-voz da Google, em uma mensagem enviada à AFP. "Estudaremos as conclusões da agência e seguiremos suas recomendações", acrescentou. Graças a um clima ameno, uma eletricidade relativamente estável e barata, produzida majoritariamente mediante energia nuclear, além de uma ampla capacidade eólica e hidrelétrica, a Finlândia experimentou recentemente um auge dos investimentos em "data centers".

artigo.texto: Three Georgia Democratic state office candidates discussed their views on environmental policy regarding data centers, renewable energy and water on Tuesday, Oct. 6, at the Forum on Energy and the Environment at the Athens-Clarke County library. The candidates were Suzanna Karatassos, running for House District 120, Eric Gisler, running for re-election in House District 121 and Ray Smith, running for Senate District 46. The forum had scripted and audience-submitted questions – the majority of which involved data centers and their effects on local communities. There were around 40 audience members. The candidates all opposed data centers, but differed in how they should be dealt with. “First and foremost, we need to stop the harm that’s being done,” Smith said. Smith said the first course of action should be to pass a moratorium on data center construction until there are safeguards in place, and consider community benefit agreements in legislation around construction. He also discussed how the centers should be covering the full costs of upgrades to transmission systems, and that the centers should pay for the large share of electricity they use. “[Data centers] don’t have to be harmful,” Smith said. “The data centers that are being built right now are massive, and have a very large impact and footprint. … They could be 100% renewable. They could be building their own renewable energy to cover their own needs, and they're not doing that.” Smith mentioned how projects the size of data centers should not be built without the knowledge of local governments, and that believes the state could provide more guidance to local governments. Gisler does not support an immediate moratorium on data center construction, but sees another solution. "What we're doing right now is giving massive tax breaks to attract these data centers to come [to Georgia],” Gisler said. “There's a lot of things we could do to try to rein [data centers] in a bit and [we] start … by repealing that tax credit.” He emphasized that while tax breaks are at the state level, local communities are affected just as much because local property and sales taxes are also credited.He also called for more water regulation, for data centers to pay for the power grid infrastructure themselves, for transparency from the government about data centers and for incentives for centers to use clean energy. Karatassos called for a moratorium on data centers for one year, and for more regulating legislation to be passed. “I see data centers as pure capitalism, and it’s up to the states, the legislators, to regulate them,” Karatassos said. She also believes data centers should be in industrial zones to prevent them from being constructed in residential or natural locations. Karatassos agreed with the previous candidates about cutting tax incentives. All three candidates believe, according to their comments, there should be room for public comment in regards to data centers.

artigo.texto: SMM, October 8: During the National Day holiday, the sodium-ion battery industry chain largely maintained its pre-holiday pattern, with no notable changes. On the materials side, major cathode enterprises carried out staggered production as scheduled: some began maintenance shutdowns from mid-holiday, with toll processing entities stepping in to ensure supply continuity, leaving core client order deliveries unaffected; construction of newly contracted 10kt-scale production lines progressed normally. On the anode side, some enterprises proceeded with debugging of new production lines and trial production preparations as planned, with the pace unchanged—targeting production readiness by late October and batch delivery by mid-November. Raw material prices were broadly stable during the holiday, with phosphorus-based materials holding at post-pullback lows, bamboo-based material prices steady, and coconut shell charcoal maintaining pre-holiday levels. On the battery cell side, the "September-October peak season" delivery pace continued, grid connection of energy storage projects before year-end remained a clear priority, and mainstream product prices held near 0.6 Yuan/Wh, with no new price adjustments. Industry attention around the holiday did not fade but shifted to three periods: first, whether new anode production lines can start on schedule in late October; second, progress on the launch and validation of 180Ah energy-density products; and third, Q4 order fulfillment. Overall, the industry is in a phase of "steady transition, poised for momentum," with the holiday leaving the tight supply-demand balance fundamentally unchanged. artigo.texto: South African Energy Storage Association (SAESA) welcomes 4,600 MW battery storage prioritisation and calls for integrated energy planning The South African Energy Storage Association (SAESA) (www.SAESA.org.za) welcomes the prioritisation of 4,600 MW of battery energy storage under the first Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) 2025 Section 34 determination. The timing is significant. Recent Integrated Energy Plan (IEP) modelling and assumptions discussions highlighted a fundamental shift that South Africa’s energy planning now needs to capture: we cannot plan the future power system by counting megawatts of generation alone. We must plan for when energy is available, where it is available, how it moves through a constrained grid and how it is stored and dispatched when the system needs it most. The announcement reinforces that shift. Battery energy storage systems (BESS) are becoming critical system infrastructure, supporting flexibility, reducing avoidable curtailment, shifting energy into periods of demand and strengthening security of supply. For SAESA, the message for the IEP is clear: storage, flexibility and system services must be modelled as integral components of South Africa’s future electricity architecture, with their contribution considered from the outset of generation planning. “The IEP must plan the power system we are becoming, not simply model the power system we have inherited,” says SAESA. Partnership with C&I Energy + Storage Summit SAESA is an association partner of the C&I Energy + Storage Summit, created by VUKA Group, taking place on 28–29 October 2026 at The Maslow Hotel, Sandton, Johannesburg. The summit brings together commercial and industrial energy users, project developers, financiers, regulators and solution providers to explore practical approaches to energy security, procurement and storage deployment. For businesses assessing how storage can support their operations, the event offers an opportunity to meet SAESA and engage with the wider energy community on the decisions shaping South Africa’s evolving electricity system. Commercial and industrial energy decision-makers are invited to apply to attend as hosted buyers. Qualifying buyers receive complimentary summit access and curated opportunities to engage with industry partners. Meet SAESA at C&I Energy + Storage Summit: Join the Hosted Buyer Programme The Hosted Buyer Programme connects commercial and industrial energy decision-makers with solution providers shaping South Africa’s evolving private energy market. Qualified energy buyers receive complimentary access to the summit and curated engagement with industry partners exploring energy procurement, storage deployment and project development. Apply for the Hosted Buyer Programme (https://apo-opa.co/4ehLijJ) Distributed by APO Group on behalf of VUKA Group. About SAESA: The South African Energy Storage Association (SAESA) is the national trade association dedicated to advancing energy storage. It works towards a more resilient, efficient, sustainable and affordable electricity system through industry advocacy, knowledge sharing and support for its members’ business development. www.SAESA.org.za About the C&I Energy + Storage Summit: The C&I Energy + Storage Summit connects commercial and industrial energy users with project developers, financiers, regulators and solution providers to address the practical challenges shaping South Africa’s private energy market. Organised by VUKA Group, the Johannesburg edition takes place on 28–29 October 2026 at The Maslow Hotel, Sandton, alongside the EIUG Conference, Water Security Africa and the Data Centre Summit. https://apo-opa.co/4ziszNa About VUKA Group: VUKA Group connects people and organisations with information, industry networks and business opportunities across Africa. Through its events and media platforms, the group brings stakeholders together to share knowledge, build relationships and support the growth of the industries it serves. Its power and energy portfolio includes Enlit Africa, the C&I Energy + Storage Summit, Water Security Africa and ESI Africa. www.WeAreVuka.com Distributed via APO Group / Africa Newsroom View original ↗

artigo.texto: Mumbai: The BEST undertaking is set to introduce a new generation of electric buses powered by Blade Battery technology, with the first batch of 25 buses expected to enter service by the end of October. Supplied by Olectra Greentech, the buses are designed to offer a longer range, improved safety and lower operating costs. Batteries Integrated Into Chassis The buses use lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries integrated into the chassis. The lightweight battery system can store at least 30 per cent more energy than batteries currently used in existing air-conditioned electric buses. The buses are expected to operate for up to two days on a single charge, potentially reducing charging requirements and improving fleet availability. A senior Olectra Greentech official said the Blade Battery is designed to withstand extreme climatic conditions and remains safer even when severely damaged in accidents. “It has very slow heat generation and no oxygen release,” the official said, adding that its compact design improves space utilisation in the battery pack by more than 50 per cent. The technology is already being used in electric buses in cities such as London and Singapore. For BEST, the rollout comes as the undertaking expands its electric fleet to meet Mumbai’s growing public transport demand. artigo.texto: SMM, October 7: Key points: During the National Day holiday, the solid-state battery sector showed a pattern of “hot policy, slow industry.” Seven ministries’ 15th Five-Year Plan set 2030 as the target for large-scale application of all-solid-state batteries; Sinocera’s sulphide production line was completed, Chuneng’s polymer GWh-level line went into operation, and a 100 GWh project was signed. Overseas, Samsung SDI/EcoPro cooperation and BMW real-vehicle validation moved forward. However, materials are seeing “rising volumes and falling prices,” and the transition from pilot production to mass production still requires 2–3 years, with cost reduction, yield, and client validation remaining the three major hurdles. Around the National Day holiday, the solid-state battery industry received a dual boost from “policy direction” and “industrial implementation.” Many enterprises arranged early holiday breaks, and actual industrial implementation remained slow. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and six other departments jointly issued the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the New-Type Battery Industry, setting a 2030 timetable for the large-scale application of all-solid-state batteries for the first time in a national-level special plan. At the same time, China’s first polymer GWh-level production line went into operation, Sinocera Materials’ sulphide electrolyte production line was completed, and a project with over 100 GWh of capacity was signed. The industry is accelerating its transition from an “intensive pilot phase” to a “mass-production validation phase.” However, SMM believes there remains a clear gap between policy enthusiasm and industrial reality—the trend of “rising volumes and falling prices” on the materials side has not yet reversed, and the window from pilot production to mass production still requires 2–3 years of validation. I. Policy side: First national-level special plan released, 2030 timetable officially set During this holiday, the biggest variable for the solid-state battery industry came from the policy side. On September 28, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and six other departments jointly issued the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the New-Type Battery Industry. This is China’s first national-level special plan in the battery sector, explicitly proposing that by 2030 all-solid-state batteries will achieve initial large-scale application, and top-tier players’ product defect rates will reach the PPB (1 part per billion) level. Notably, the plan places special emphasis on key technology directions such as interface contact, high ionic conductivity, long cycle life, and engineered pressure system design, while also proposing to promote the integrated application of high-voltage cathode materials and new-type lithium metal-based anode materials. This indicates that policy orientation has shifted from “encouraging R&D” to “engineering implementation,” targeting the core bottlenecks in the industrialisation of all-solid-state batteries. II. Materials side: Sulphide electrolytes see “rising volumes and falling prices,” capacity construction enters the “mt era” The core highlight on the materials side during this holiday was the acceleration of capacity construction and the continued downward shift of the price center. Sinocera Materials’ sulphide electrolyte production line completed. On October 5, Sinocera Materials disclosed that its automated sulphide solid-state electrolyte production line had been successfully completed, with initial mass-production capability established. The first line is planned to have an annual capacity of 30 mt and is expected to be completed and put into operation within 2026; the second line is planned to have an annual capacity of 100 mt and will be advanced in an orderly manner based on the industrialisation pace of downstream battery enterprises. It is worth noting that Sinocera Materials is simultaneously laying out both oxide and sulphide technology routes, but its current strategic center is focused on the sulphide route, and its product performance has been highly recognised by downstream battery enterprises. SMM believes that sulphide electrolytes are in the typical early-industry stage of "rising volume and falling prices"—production is increasing, but capacity utilization rates remain low, and price pressure has been the dominant theme since Q3. The commissioning of 100 mt-class production lines means the industry is crossing from the "kg-class" to the "mt-class" threshold, but there is still some distance from truly meaningful large-scale supply. III. Battery cell side: Polymer route achieves GWh-class breakthrough, "three dominant players" landscape begins to emerge In battery cell manufacturing, the most noteworthy event this holiday is the GWh-class mass production breakthrough on the polymer route. China's first polymer solid-state battery GWh-class production line has been commissioned. On 29 September, Chunlv New Energy's Hukou 1 GWh solid-state battery intelligent manufacturing base officially entered production, marking China's first solid-state battery mass production line using the polymer process route. The project is planned to be built in two phases, with total capacity reaching 5 GWh once fully ramped up, covering diverse scenarios including grid-side ESS, industrial and commercial ESS, passenger NEVs, drones, robots, and marine power. The industrial significance of this event is that it breaks the long-standing "sulphide + oxide" dual-route dominance in the solid-state battery industry and validates the industrial manufacturing strength of the polymer route. The solid-state battery industry has officially entered a new competitive landscape of three dominant players: sulphide, oxide, and polymer. artigo.texto: A Core Stack, braço de infraestrutura digital do Lazzari Group, e a Green Arrow Capital anunciaram um plano de investimento superior a €1 bilhão ao longo de quatro anos na Itália. O projeto prevê a construção de 13 data centers de médio porte, abastecidos por energia renovável gerada nos próprios locais. Segundo as empresas, as primeiras unidades serão instaladas nas províncias de Cremona e Verona. A expectativa é obter as licenças necessárias até o fim de 2027 e iniciar as operações no primeiro trimestre de 2028. Após os projetos mais avançados no norte e nordeste italianos, o plano deverá avançar para as regiões centro-sul. As companhias também afirmaram que o desenvolvimento utilizará uma cadeia de fornecedores inteiramente italiana. Principais fatos e números - O investimento previsto supera €1 bilhão em quatro anos. - O plano contempla 13 data centers de médio porte na Itália. - As unidades deverão usar energia renovável gerada no próprio local. - Os dois primeiros projetos ficam nas províncias de Cremona e Verona. - As licenças iniciais são esperadas até o fim de 2027. - O início das primeiras operações está previsto para o primeiro trimestre de 2028. Por que isso importa para empresários e investidores O projeto pode abrir oportunidades para fornecedores italianos de construção, equipamentos, energia e serviços ligados à infraestrutura digital, já que as empresas dizem pretender usar uma cadeia integralmente nacional. A expansão também sinaliza demanda por capacidade computacional distribuída além dos principais polos do norte do país. Para investidores e parceiros, porém, o cronograma permanece sujeito à obtenção de licenças e à execução dos aportes anunciados. Ainda não foram informados a capacidade energética de cada unidade, a divisão dos investimentos entre os locais nem contratos com futuros clientes, o que limita a avaliação do retorno e da escala operacional.

artigo.texto: A australiana AirTrunk pretende elevar para até US$ 30 bilhões seu investimento total em data centers no Japão durante os próximos cinco anos, segundo declaração de seu fundador e CEO, Robin Khuda, ao Nikkei Asia. O montante representa cerca de três vezes o investimento da operadora no país. Apoiada pela Blackstone, a empresa busca ampliar sua capacidade para atender ao aumento da demanda por infraestrutura de inteligência artificial na Ásia. Khuda afirmou que os clientes aceitam pagar um valor adicional para instalar capacidade de processamento no mercado japonês. O executivo também avalia que a Ásia pode ser a principal beneficiária de uma eventual desaceleração dos Estados Unidos, embora os dados fornecidos não detalhem os projetos, o cronograma dos aportes nem as fontes de financiamento. Principais fatos e números - A AirTrunk planeja investir até US$ 30 bilhões no Japão em cinco anos. - O valor projetado triplicaria o investimento total da empresa no país. - A expansão busca atender à demanda por infraestrutura de inteligência artificial na Ásia. - Robin Khuda disse que clientes aceitam pagar mais para instalar capacidade no Japão. - A operadora australiana de data centers é apoiada pela Blackstone. Por que isso importa para empresários e investidores O plano indica uma expansão relevante da infraestrutura digital japonesa e pode abrir oportunidades para fornecedores de energia, equipamentos, refrigeração, construção e serviços de conectividade. Para empresas que utilizam inteligência artificial, a oferta adicional de capacidade local pode ampliar alternativas de implantação no Japão, embora não haja informação sobre preços futuros ou datas de entrada em operação. Investidores devem considerar os riscos de execução de um programa de até US$ 30 bilhões, incluindo a disponibilidade de energia e a concretização da demanda. A fonte não informa localidades, projetos específicos, estrutura financeira ou compromissos já contratados.

artigo.texto: ATHENS — The town of Athens wants a little more time to think about the industries it wants to welcome within its borders. The town board moved Monday to allow Supervisor Michael Pirrone, if he deems necessary, to extend moratoriums on cannabis farming, data centers and battery-energy storage into next year. "It is always a proper approach to take things at the proper pace to evaluate all the current information, research available," Pirrone said Tuesday. "This way it will stimulate input from the people. That helps us make better decisions." He added the decision to review the bans together helps him keep a "handle" on their deadlines. The longest-standing moratorium, which covers the development of battery facilities, may extend into its third year as the town seeks to pass a local law regulating their development. Ahead of an approval vote, the town will hold a public hearing on the issue at the Rivertown Senior Center at 6 p.m. Oct. 19. Battery-energy storage facilities The soonest priority of the three industry for Athens is establishing guidelines for battery-energy storage facilities within the town. The current draft of local law No. 5 of 2026 seeks to "regulate the siting, design, installation, operation and decommissioning of battery energy storage systems." Athens is looking to hold facilities to storing a limit of 400 kilo-watt hours, to create a specific zoning district and to establish emergency response plans among other requirements. If Pirrone sees it valuable, the moratorium, set to expire Dec. 1, could be extended until June 1, 2027. "(The moratorium) was the result of people coming to us at meetings and telling us about the dangers and issues with battery storage facilities," he said, especially concerning potential fires. New York suffered from four battery-energy storage facility fires in 2023. The federal Environmental Protection Agency advises battery fires to be isolated and managed rather than put out. The EPA reports the rate of fires dropped 98% to 0.03 fires per installed gigawatt in 2024 from 1.5 fires per gigawatt in 2018, while gaining nearly 300 gigawatts of storage in the same timeframe. "These are all things the town has been concerned about," Pirrone said. The moratorium on such facilities was initially established March 4, 2024, amid public outcry that eventually halted the development of a storage facility in the town of Catskill. Eolian Energy withdrew its application for a battery-energy storage system Nov. 6, 2024, citing the negative reception from residents of Catskill. "Unfortunately, the actions taken by the planning board showed us that the community was not yet ready for this step into a cleaner and more secure energy future," according to the company's letter of withdrawal. Pirrone said Tuesday he doesn't want to see the same fiasco in Athens. He said the board has spent the last two-plus years gathering information to develop a law before potential applications are considered. "We feel that we have a more-than-adequate law that we hope will pass," he said. Cannabis farming The town's temporary ban on commercial cannabis cultivation is its newest. Pirrone, in June, described the moratorium as preemptive because of a lack of zoning regulations in the town. The municipality has received some inquiries from potential growers to create farms ahead of its decision to pause development June 15. "The town is a farming community and is seeing how cannabis farming fits under the general terms of farming in the town, and adopting the proper regulations for it," Pirrone said in June. On Tuesday, he said time is still needed to gather the facts around zoning regulations and other issues. The current moratorium, set to expire Dec. 15, could be extended by Pirrone to June 15, 2027. "We're looking to make sure we have the right information, and also the state has the right procedures for someone to operate," he said. Data centers There's not much need for the town to extend its moratorium on data centers, but Athens may do it anyway, Pirrone said. "We just want to make sure we keep it in front of our eyes," he said. Gov. Kathy Hochul established a one-year statewide moratorium on the development of new hyperscale data centers July 14. In the meantime, the state is working to make money available for communities and repeal sales-tax exemptions for data centers. Athens established its one-year moratorium Dec. 1, 2025, seven months before Hochul's moratorium. An extension by Pirrone would last until May 30, 2027. He said Tuesday a pause independent from the state's may continue to be necessary. "It's very important for me as the supervisor to do all I can to ensure the safety and the welfare of all residents within the town of Athens," Pirrone said.

artigo.texto: COLUMBIA — The city of Columbia's planning and zoning commission held its final work session before beginning to draft regulations for a possible new data center. Thursday was the sixth meeting on data centers, and commission members considered various factors like electricity, water and zoning concerns. While the amendments will soon begin to be drafted, there are still multiple steps to take before the regulations are presented to city council. So far, the commission has set forth some dates for the next stages. David Kunz, a senior planner with the community development department in the planning division, said that while most of the dates are scheduled, they could be pushed back. "We want to have a good draft, not just a draft," Kunz said. "It may take time, but I think the input we've gathered from the commission has been helpful. I think we have some good discretion at this point." Columbia Planning and Zoning commissioners reviewed possible criteria for where data centers could be built in Columbia. On Oct. 22, the commission will review online feedback it collected from community members. Some of the feedback from residents that will be reviewed includes their opinions on what the rules for data centers will be, who should pay for the data center and their expectations for transparency. At the end of this year, city employees are set to draft their regulations and meet to discuss them on Dec. 10. On Jan. 7, 2027, a presentation on the regulation draft is set to have a public hearing with the commission. After presenting the draft to the commission and receiving approval, it will then go to the city council for an introduction and then a decision. A data center moratorium was approved in Columbia earlier this year. This means a new data center cannot be built in the city until May 2027. Missouri has 95 data centers, with five in Columbia.

artigo.texto: China corre para construir centros de dados em busca da supremacia em IA O esforço está criando grandes novos polos de computação, como Ulanqab, na Mongólia Interior, onde 89 centros de dados já foram construídos ou estão planejados. A expansão da infraestrutura de IA está entre as mais rápidas do mundo Atualizado 08/10/2026 A China está construindo centros de dados em ritmo acelerado em seu interior rico em energia, com Pequim tentando transformar a abundância de eletricidade e as terras baratas em uma vantagem na corrida pelo desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial. O esforço está criando grandes novos polos de computação, como Ulanqab, na Mongólia Interior, onde 89 centros de dados já foram construídos ou estão planejados. A expansão da infraestrutura de IA está entre as mais rápidas do mundo. Pequim definiu o avanço da IA como uma prioridade estratégica nacional, como forma de aumentar a produtividade econômica, consolidar a influência política interna e assegurar a influência global da China, garantindo que uma parcela cada vez maior do mundo dependa da sua tecnologia. Embora a China tenha dificuldades para obter chips avançados em quantidade suficiente para atender à demanda crescente por IA, o país conseguiu mobilizar as terras, a eletricidade e a capacidade de construção necessárias para erguer os centros de dados que abrigam esses chips. A China já dispõe de 24 gigawatts de capacidade operacional de computação em centros de dados, mais que o restante da Ásia somado, mas menos da metade dos 56 GW dos Estados Unidos, segundo a SemiAnalysis, consultoria especializada em chips. Outros 50 GW estão em construção ou foram anunciados. Ulanqab, uma remota cidade agrícola conhecida por suas batatas e petiscos de iogurte, está entre os exemplos mais marcantes dessa expansão. Cerca de 15 GW de capacidade de computação foram destinados à cidade, tornando-a o polo de centros de dados que mais cresce na Ásia, segundo um executivo de uma importante operadora do setor na região, que preferiu não se identificar devido à sensibilidade do tema. A cidade vem se beneficiando de vantagens cada vez mais escassas em outros mercados: abundância de energia eólica e de carvão, terras baratas, clima frio e capacidade de construir instalações rapidamente. Isso contrasta com os EUA, onde garantir eletricidade e conexões à rede elétrica se tornou uma das principais limitações à expansão dos centros de dados. Escola abandonada Engenheiros estão até transformando uma escola secundária abandonada em um centro de dados. A operadora ZData assumiu o campus depois que a escola foi fechada, à medida que o número de matrículas caiu junto com a redução da população regional em idade escolar. Em breve, fileiras de racks de computação ocuparão o pátio onde os alunos passavam o intervalo entre as aulas. A dimensão das obras é visível nos arredores da cidade. O “Financial Times” constatou obras em andamento de pelo menos uma dúzia de empresas em quatro grandes complexos de centros de dados, com algumas operadoras construindo instalações em vários locais. Alibaba e Huawei Entre elas estão a Alibaba e a Huawei, além de operadores como ZData e VNET, que constroem instalações e alugam capacidade de computação para empresas de tecnologia. A ByteDance se tornou a maior fonte de demanda da China por infraestrutura alugada de computação, enquanto os laboratórios de IA DeepSeek e Z.ai também estão construindo instalações em Ulanqab, segundo fontes informadas sobre o assunto. A Z.ai não respondeu a um pedido para comentar. Eric Xu, presidente rotativo da Huawei, que possui três centros de dados em Ulanqab, diz que a gigante tecnológica avaliou vários locais antes de escolher a cidade, devido à eletricidade barata e a proximidade com Pequim, a apenas duas horas de trem de alta velocidade. “Eu achava que era uma cidade pequena”, afirma Xu, que viajou a Ulanqab pela primeira vez em agosto. “Fiquei surpreso com seu tamanho. É muito diferente do que eu esperava.” A Mongólia Interior tinha 117 GW de capacidade instalada de energia eólica em junho deste ano, o maior parque eólico da China e quase quatro vezes toda a capacidade eólica do Reino Unido. A região também tem cerca de 130 GW de capacidade de geração de energia a partir de combustíveis fósseis, em sua maioria usinas a carvão. David Fishman, analista de energia da consultoria The Lantau Group, diz que a Mongólia Interior provavelmente tem “o maior excedente local de eletricidade” de qualquer região administrativa do mundo. “Há uma quantidade imensa de eletricidade sendo gerada com taxas de utilização muito baixas. Os centros de dados ajudam a absorver esse excedente de energia”, acrescenta ele. Atualmente, os centros de dados de Ulanqab pagam cerca de 0,358 yuan por quilowatt-hora de eletricidade, ante preços médio de mais de 0,60 yuan por kWh para a indústria em muitas cidades chinesas e de cerca de 0,80 yuan por kWh em Pequim. O clima frio da região também ajuda a reduzir as enormes necessidades de refrigeração dos clusters de computação de IA. As temperaturas médias anuais em Ulanqab são de cerca de 4,3ºC, enquanto a proximidade com Pequim permite que as equipes de engenharia cheguem rapidamente aos locais. A Mongólia Interior também tem a vantagem de contar com um grau incomum de flexibilidade quanto à forma de fornecimento de energia para grandes projetos de computação. Enquanto a maior parte da China é atendida pela Rede Estatal, a concessionária nacional de eletricidade, o oeste da Mongólia Interior é atendido pela Mengxi Power Grid, que opera de forma independente. artigo.texto: Chinese New Energy Vehicle Startups Are Collectively Venturing Into the Deep Waters of the Battery Sector The crazy September saw a boom of automakers' in-house R&D on batteries. On September 4, Xiaomi released its Longjia Battery and announced partnerships with CALB and Sunwoda Power; on September 7, Li Auto announced that its in-house developed batteries will be gradually installed on all its vehicle models; on September 16, Leapmotor claimed that it has achieved 100% in-house R&D of battery cells; the next day, He Xiaopeng, Chairman of XPeng, stated at the G9L launch event: "Starting from this year, XPeng will develop all its batteries on its own." * Source: Xiaomi The motivation behind in-house R&D is that automakers no longer want to be mere battery buyers. Most of their previous battery budgets went to CATL, the king of batteries. Spending money is not the top concern — the fact that the right to define battery solutions and the initiative of the supply chain are in the hands of others keeps some automakers up at night. As a result, some call this a "de-CATL" trend, while others argue that "in-house R&D" is just a new guise. Judging from various incidents in the battery industry in the past, in-house R&D is far from being that simple. 01 "The auto industry camp stages a collective 'rebellion'" The direct reason for automakers to extend their reach to the battery industry chain is that they do not want to "pour too much money" into battery suppliers. In 2022, Zeng Qinghong, then Chairman of GAC Group, publicly stated that battery costs accounted for 40% to 60% of the total vehicle cost, and uttered the famous line: "Aren't we just working for CATL?" Objectively speaking, CATL's profit performance does make automakers extremely sensitive to the distribution of benefits across the industrial chain. Financial reports show that in the first half of this year, CATL's net profit reached 47.031 billion yuan, up 45.31% year on year, with a net profit margin of about 16%. In contrast, the total net profit of 15 mainstream automakers listed on the A-share and Hong Kong stock markets was only 21.048 billion yuan, and a large number of automakers have a net profit margin of less than 5%. * Source: Xueqiu Thus, conflicts emerge. Automakers have to bear the pressure of vehicle price competition and sales, while a large part of battery procurement costs is determined by the supply chain. Battery prices can rise along with upstream raw material costs, but automakers dare not raise vehicle prices arbitrarily, otherwise it will arouse consumers' resentment and do more harm than good. Tiny fluctuations in battery procurement prices can directly determine whether an automaker makes a profit or loss, which in the eyes of automakers is an unbearable inversion of power. Not only that, at this stage, if automakers want to truly develop their own differentiated products, they have to delve deep into battery development inevitably. In the past, battery procurement was largely similar to "off-the-shelf selection". Suppliers provided mature products, and automakers selected products according to requirements for cruising range, interior space and cost, then completed vehicle adaptation. Even if the two sides carried out joint development, the openness of material formulas, manufacturing parameters and production data still depended on the specific cooperative relationship. * Source: Internet However, with the development of 800V high-voltage platforms, ultra-fast charging and cell-to-chassis (CTC) integration technologies, such boundary is increasingly difficult to maintain. The "three core electric systems" today are equivalent to engines and gearboxes in the era of fuel vehicles, belonging to core technologies that directly affect the final user experience of vehicles: The structure of the battery pack affects cabin space, total vehicle weight and body rigidity; thermal management affects continuous fast charging capability; the battery management system affects cruising range estimation, power output and service life. Batteries are deeply coupled with the vehicle architecture. If automakers want to define products in depth, they have to rely on battery enterprises, which is unacceptable for them. Therefore, among the latest batch of in-house R&D cases, the change in the relationship between automakers and suppliers is the most obvious. The Longjia Battery released by Xiaomi on September 4 is led by Xiaomi in battery pack design and development, and Xiaomi participates in in-depth R&D of battery cells with its partners. CALB and Sunwoda Power provide battery cell R&D and manufacturing capabilities, while Xiaomi participates in product definition and vehicle adaptation. He Xiaopeng commented on in-house R&D like this: "It's not just about battery cells. Investing in battery cell companies still leaves the core technology in others' hands. We have also invested in three battery cell enterprises, but starting from this year, we will develop all batteries on our own." * Source: Internet According to public information, the three companies are most likely CALB, Sunwoda and SVOLT. XPeng mainly carries out in-house R&D and manufacturing of battery pack systems, while battery cells are led by its partners, whose purpose is to increase supply sources to grasp more initiative. It can be seen that this collective "rebellion" is essentially a move by vehicle enterprises to change their right to speak in the industrial chain. As for whether they can become real definers, it depends on how much capability they master, rather than how loud slogans they shout. 02 "After technology popularization, in-house R&D becomes a bargaining chip" The reason why automakers can enter the battery field today is related to the gradual maturity of mainstream technical routes and the increasing number of battery supplier options. At present, both lithium iron phosphate and ternary lithium batteries have formed mature industrialization route
