artigo.texto: COLORADO SPRINGS, Colorado — Billions of dollars in data center construction are generating significant insurance demand, but a growing challenge for insurers is the accumulation of exposures rather than a broad shortage of capacity, insurance executives say. Most projects can obtain the property and builders risk capacity they need, but insurers and reinsurers must track overlapping construction, operational property, equipment and power exposures, they said. The executives spoke this week at the Insurance Leadership Forum, sponsored by the Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers. The boom has sparked public opposition in some states over concerns about electricity and water use and the effect on local communities, prompting proposals to restrict or pause some developments. Despite the pushback, insurance executives at the conference generally described data centers as a major growth opportunity for the industry. Thousands of data centers are expected to be developed globally, with many projects valued between $3 billion and $5 billion, said Ryan Barber, New York-based global head of property at Aon. There is ample capacity for projects of that size, which are generally highly engineered and attractive property risks, he said. “We’ve done placements now with limits as high as $8.5 billion, and that was over a year ago; we could probably do placements in excess of $10 billion now,” Mr. Barber said. Aon is developing an operational property insurance facility for data centers. Aon estimates data centers could generate more than $100 billion in new insurance premiums over the next five to 10 years, he said. But rapid development is creating accumulation issues as large campuses are built in phases, leaving insurers with builders risk and operational property exposures at the same site, Mr. Barber said. Other exposures can include high-value computer equipment and dedicated power generation, increasing the potential for insurers and reinsurers to accumulate exposures to the same projects. “The biggest struggle right now for insurers and reinsurers, for that matter, is to just track and understand the accumulation of risk that they’re taking on from these data centers,” Mr. Barber said. Managing aggregation is also an important consideration in site and insurer selection, said Pat Donnelly, Chicago-based head of risk and broking for North America at Willis. Some insurers can provide coverage across several phases of a development, while others prefer individual segments, he said. Insurers must consider those exposures alongside property risks already on their books, said Marc Orloff, Boston-based president of global risk solutions North America at Liberty Mutual. “We all write a lot of property already … so it’s all about managing tolerances. How much of our exposure do we want? How much volatility do we want on our balance sheets?” he said. Concentrations of expensive data centers in areas exposed to severe convective storms add to the uncertainty, Mr. Orloff said. Property and business interruption capacity remains plentiful for most projects, but capacity in other lines is more constrained, said Marc Kunney, San Francisco-based chief client officer at EPIC Insurance Brokers & Consultants. “Where some of the challenges are is on the professional liability, which is a much more limited marketplace,” Mr. Kunney said. The construction boom is generating substantial premium, but not all of the revenue will recur once projects are completed, Mr. Orloff said. Operational property coverage may generate lower premium volumes, while builders risk premium will decline if construction slows, he said. “It’s not a recurring revenue stream,” Mr. Orloff said.

artigo.texto: Fayette County residents push back on data center zoning plan Opponents call for extended moratorium, stricter limits on hyperscale facilities LEXINGTON, Ky. (WKYT) - Fayette County residents voiced opposition Tuesday to hyperscale data centers and current zoning recommendations put forth earlier this year by the planning commission. “I expect for my council, my representatives to represent me. Not big industry,” one resident said. Opponents cite risks, demand moratorium extension Opponents said that if the draft moves forward, anticipated noise, water, energy, financial and air quality impacts will put communities at risk. Those opposed overwhelmingly demanded a two-year extension of the moratorium and a complete ban of centers larger than 25 megawatts if evidence discovered in those two years points to negative impacts. “Other safety critical industries such as transportation, energy, medicine and weapons are regulated and monitored. AI needs to be treated the same,” one speaker said. Other demands included a cap on data center license issuances, incentives to use lower carbon emission fuels, cutting the decibel limit to 25, and changing zoning rules to limit a center by its utility intake rather than square footage. Some also called for a one-year extension of the data center moratorium. Some see economic opportunity Others in attendance Tuesday said they see AI and data centers as drivers of economic growth in the future and do not wish to jeopardize it. “Data infrastructure is critically important. Data technology, having that infrastructure here is as essential to economic development today as sites and buildings, as water and sewer, and broadband capacity,” one speaker said. Developer addresses concerns Several speakers noted data center developer DART Point’s recent acquisition of more than 300,000 square feet of property to create a data center campus. A DART Point representative addressed resource-based concerns. “We’re not a threat on the noise factor, the water system we use will be a closed loop system, and the power, we already have it,” the representative said. Urban County Council members said they will continue discussions on data centers at the next meeting, including where any potential projects could be developed and how the data centers would be used. The possibility of a one-year extension of the moratorium will also be discussed. Copyright 2026 WKYT. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: FCL-X Fire & Safety to Showcase Advanced Lithium-Ion Battery Fire Protection Solutions at The Battery Show North America 2026 in Detroit - FCL-X Fire & Safety to exhibit atThe Battery Show North America 2026, October 13–15, atHuntington Place inDetroit, Michigan -- Booth 1629. - The Company will showcase its proprietary FCL-X™ lithium-ion battery fire extinguishing technology and integrated fire safety solutions for battery manufacturers, electric vehicle OEMs, energy storage operators, and industrial facilities. - Participation follows growing commercial momentum, including the Company's recently announced Integrated Safety Purchase Order with Kia Georgia , supporting its expansion into battery-related safety infrastructure. - The Battery Show offers direct engagement with thousands of engineers, manufacturers, technology providers, and decision-makers across the rapidly expanding North American battery and electrification sectors. TORONTO , Oct. 8, 2026 /CNW/ -- FCL-X Fire & Safety Inc. ("FFS" or the "Company") (TSXV: FCLX) (OTCQB: FCLIF) (FSE: K0Q), a U.S.-based manufacturer of lithium-ion battery fire safety products and services, is pleased to announce its participation as an exhibitor at The Battery Show North America 2026, taking place October 12–15, 2026, at Huntington Place in Detroit, Michigan. The Company will be exhibiting at Booth 1629 during the exhibition, showcasing its proprietary FCL-X™ lithium-ion battery fire extinguishing technology and expanding portfolio of integrated fire protection and safety solutions. The Battery Show North America is one of the continent's premier gatherings for advanced battery technology, electric vehicles, and energy storage innovation. The 2026 event is expected to bring together more than 16,000 industry professionals, approximately 1,000 exhibitors, and leading representatives from battery manufacturers, automotive OEMs, engineering companies, and technology developers. The Company's participation comes at an important time as the accelerating adoption of lithium-ion batteries across transportation, manufacturing, energy storage, and industrial applications continues to create demand for specialized fire protection technologies and comprehensive safety infrastructure. Building Momentum Across the Battery Safety Industry FCL-X Fire & Safety continues to strengthen its position as a specialized provider of lithium-ion battery fire protection technologies and services. The Company's proprietary FCL-X™ technology is designed to rapidly extinguish lithium-ion battery fires, provide effective cooling, help control thermal runaway, and reduce the risk of reignition. The Company has also broadened its commercial offering beyond fire extinguishing products to include integrated safety services, risk assessment, fire protection engineering, and Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) support for complex battery-related operating environments. Most recently, FCL-X Fire & Safety announced an Integrated Safety Purchase Order with Kia Georgia, Inc., covering construction support and HSE-related services at its West Point, Georgia facility. This engagement represents another important milestone in the Company's evolution toward becoming an integrated safety partner to organizations operating in battery-intensive industries. Carlos Vicens, CEO & Director of FCL-X Fire & Safety, commented: "The Battery Show brings together the companies and decision-makers who are driving the future of electrification. As battery technology advances and deployment accelerates, fire safety must evolve alongside it. We believe that effective lithium-ion battery fire protection is becoming an essential component of battery manufacturing, energy storage, electric vehicle operations, and the broader electrification ecosystem. "Our participation in Detroit provides us with an excellent opportunity to introduce FCL-X™ and our broader safety capabilities directly to the manufacturers, engineers, and operators who are building and managing these critical technologies. Following our recent engagement with Kia Georgia, we are increasingly focused on positioning FCL-X Fire & Safety as an integrated safety solutions partner for the battery industry." Addressing a Critical Challenge in Battery Manufacturing and Electrification Lithium-ion battery fires present significant challenges due to thermal runaway, extreme temperatures, the potential for cell-to-cell propagation, and the risk of reignition. artigo.texto: Data center moratorium vote postponed after fight, protests MEMPHIS, Tenn. (WMC/Gray News) — Chaos ensued during Tuesday night’s data center moratorium vote by the city council in Memphis, Tennessee. More than 100 people showed up to the meeting to hear the outcome on the proposed ordinance. “This is just a total hazard. We’ve basically been invaded by strangers, by people that have gotten paid, and they have not communicated with us in any way,” said Amber Lowe, a local community member. “This is hurtful, and I’m rethinking where I need to be living at.” The decision to delay the vote until Oct. 20 led to a fight breaking out in the lobby and tense exchanges among city council members. A fight between two women spilled into the lobby, with punches thrown while protesters chanted inside the meeting. One woman had her hair pulled and was slapped seconds later. Councilwoman Yolanda Cooper-Sutton was pulled out of the meeting after arguing with protesters and council member JB Smiley. “You could’ve came to see me like I asked you to... I ain’t no coward; you pipe down, baby, I clap back,” Cooper-Sutton said. The city council halted the meeting amid the turmoil and subsequently delayed the vote. Crowds chanted “this is our city” and “show me what democracy looks like” as the demonstration moved from the chamber into the halls of the building. Protesters said they are not done pursuing the issue. Memphis police were called to the disturbance at city hall, but a department spokesperson says no one was detained and no one was harmed. artigo.texto: Verso Energy inaugurates a 6 MW battery at its floating solar site The energy company commissions a 6 MW / 12 MWh system at Gueugnon, paired with a 23.1 MWp floating park. It is also starting a 23 MW / 46 MWh battery in the Marne. Verso Energy has inaugurated a 6 MW / 12 MWh battery storage system at its floating solar site in Gueugnon. According to the company, the installation stores electricity produced during the sunniest hours, when the grid cannot absorb everything, and releases it later. Verso Energy is simultaneously starting construction of a 23 MW / 46 MWh battery at VÃ©signeul-sur-Marne, in the Marne department. The Gueugnon site, launched in July 2025, includes a 23.1 MWp floating photovoltaic park. Huawei supplied the batteries, while CEME and Bouhet TP carried out the construction. According to Verso Energy, combining panels and batteries makes it the largest hybrid floating solar plant in France. Other players are developing comparable projects, such as Nala Renewables, which started construction of a 125 MW/250 MWh battery storage project in Finland, or EDF and NYPA, which are partnering to develop 240 MW of solar in New York. A grid that cannot absorb everything At peak sunshine, the Gueugnon plant can produce more electricity than the grid can absorb, the company says. Until the reinforcement planned by Enedis in 2028, the battery stores the midday surplus instead of dissipating it, then feeds it back later. Total investment, covering the solar plant and the batteries, stands at about â¬27 million. Company Huawei: company profile Verso Energy presents these solutions as flexibility tools, meaning the ability to shift electricity production or consumption over time. They would help balance the power system as new uses grow, including data centers, mobility, heat pumps, and hydrogen and synthetic fuel plants. Storage, a segment gaining speed for Verso Energy Battery storage has become a priority for the company, which has been accelerating in this segment since 2025. The VÃ©signeul-sur-Marne project, acquired in late 2025, is nearly four times more powerful than the Gueugnon one. Verso Energy operates these batteries with its own teams, which run the facilities and market the stored electricity, an activity known as "aggregation". The batteries are monetized in two ways: by selling electricity when demand is highest, and by providing grid services, notably maintaining the balance between production and consumption at all times. "The commissioning of this battery in Gueugnon shows our ability to combine solar production and storage, and to turn a grid constraint into an opportunity," says Antoine Huard, chief executive and co-founder of Verso Energy. He adds that this know-how should allow the company's future hydrogen and synthetic fuel plants to become flexibility tools, able to adapt their consumption to grid needs. artigo.texto: Data centers face a sweeping new power regime Lawmakers are considering forcing data centers to shoulder new costs and restrictions while speeding up the energy infrastructure needed to power the AI boom. Why it matters: The bipartisan legislation, unveiled last week, represents the most aggressive response yet from Washington to data centers amid growing backlash over their energy and environmental impacts. Driving the news: The provisions are part of broader Senate legislation aimed at speeding up permitting for energy — but make no mistake: The data-center measures are significant and would go far beyond Washington's largely voluntary efforts to date. - The bill's sponsors say it would accelerate energy development while ensuring data centers pay their share of grid upgrades. "I don't think we've seen it before," said Ari Peskoe, director of the Electricity Law Initiative at Harvard Law School, about the proposed additional costs and restrictions. - "But I don't think we've seen growth that's comparable to data centers today, and I certainly don't know any industry whose electricity usage has captured so much political attention." Between the lines: For tech companies, the bill cuts both ways. Congress would make it easier to build the energy infrastructure they need while erecting a sweeping framework aimed at keeping other electricity customers from footing the bill. "Just to be candid, having some teeth on data center accountability and ratepayer protection is just table stakes to getting a deal done," said Jane Flegal, a former White House official under President Biden and now a senior fellow at the nonprofit Searchlight Institute. The big picture: Congress has been talking about overhauling permitting for years. The AI boom has given lawmakers an urgent reason to finally act: America suddenly needs enormous amounts of new power infrastructure, fast. - Faster approvals for power plants and transmission lines could directly benefit data centers struggling to secure enough electricity for their expansion. How it works: The bill reaches into virtually every part of the relationship between large data centers and the electric grid. - Data centers would be required to pay both their share of the existing transmission network and the incremental transmission costs needed to serve them, reversing a decades-old federal pricing policy that generally prevents charging both. This is the biggie, but it doesn't stop there. - New data centers of at least 20 megawatts would have to bear the incremental costs they impose across the power system, including generation, storage, transmission and distribution. - Regulators at both the federal and state levels could charge large data centers even more than those incremental costs — and use the excess to reduce other customers' bills. - Data centers would remain on the hook for infrastructure costs even if they stop buying electricity before those costs have been recovered. Utilities would also have to secure financial guarantees before building infrastructure to serve them, protecting ratepayers if projects don't materialize. Zoom in: States are already moving aggressively to protect ratepayers, with dozens of policies pending or in place across more than half the states aimed at making data centers shoulder more of the costs of serving them. - The bill would explicitly give states wide latitude to go further, including treating data centers less favorably than other large industrial customers, competitively allocating access to electricity and requiring them to secure new power supplies or accept limits on electricity use. What they're saying: Not much publicly, yet. The Data Center Coalition, which represents companies across the industry, said it is still reviewing the legislation. - Microsoft, Google and Nvidia declined to comment, while Meta didn't respond to a request for comment. - Amazon energy policy director Craig Sundstrom said the aging grid and slow permitting are putting pressure on electricity costs, adding that the bill "could unlock the investment needed to build new generation and transmission faster." The intrigue: One tech industry official called some provisions an "unprecedented level of discriminatory treatment" for a single industry. - The official, who spoke anonymously to discuss industry deliberations, said tougher grid-connected requirements could encourage some developers to build more power systems completely off-grid instead — potentially undermining the overarching purpose of the bill. The other side: Travis Fisher, a former Trump White House energy official now at the libertarian Cato Institute, said he has "mild support" for the approach despite concerns about setting a discriminatory precedent. - He said the provisions "break new ground" at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission but are consistent with the White House's ratepayer-protection pledge many of the largest data center companies have already signed. What we're watching: Flegal said she would be "incredibly surprised" if tech companies ultimately oppose the broader package. What's next: With the Senate out of town ahead of the midterm elections, lawmakers and stakeholders have plenty of time to push for changes before a possible lame-duck debate. AI is moving fast. artigo.texto: FREELANDER Details Powertrain, Battery and All-Terrain Technology for International Left-Hand Drive FREELANDER 8 Source: GlobeNewswire ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates, Oct. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- FREELANDER has detailed the powertrain, battery, chassis and all-terrain technology of the international left-hand drive variant of FREELANDER 8, following its unveiling at the brand’s Global Brand Launch in Abu Dhabi on 29 September 2026. Developed for a wide range of driving conditions, FREELANDER 8 brings together premium quality, everyday comfort and all-terrain capability. Its electrified powertrain, adaptive chassis and intelligent terrain management are designed to support journeys ranging from urban commuting to demanding off-road environments. The figures in this release apply to the Middle East market model only; specifications vary by market and trim level. 460 kW hybrid powertrain and 110 km of all-electric range The Middle East market model combines a 2.0T Dedicated Hybrid Engine with a 34.12 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and dual-motor all-wheel drive. The system delivers up to 460 kW of peak power and 662 N·m of peak torque, with 0–100 km/h acceleration in 5.8 seconds. With a full tank and a fully charged battery, FREELANDER 8 delivers a total range of 886 km and an all-electric range of 110 km, both measured on the combined cycle. Actual range varies with driving conditions and use. The battery supports 11 kW AC charging and DC fast charging from 20% to 80% in 20 minutes or less. Dual-chamber air suspension and Continuously Controlled Damping The chassis combines dual-chamber air suspension with Continuously Controlled Damping (CCD), offering a maximum ground clearance of 266 mm. Adjustable ride height and damping help the vehicle respond to changing road conditions, supporting ride comfort on paved roads and clearance over uneven terrain. The All-Terrain Dual Lock System, combining a Virtual Central Differential Lock and an Electronic Limited-Slip Differential (e-LSD), manages torque distribution to help maintain traction on low-grip surfaces and during cross-axle conditions. Nine modes bring powertrain and chassis control together The i-ATS (Intelligent All-Terrain System) offers nine modes: seven terrain programmes, including Sand Mode, plus Smart Mode and Expert Mode. Working with the electrified powertrain and chassis, it helps the driver adapt to changing surfaces. Under the relevant test conditions, FREELANDER 8 can pass an 800 mm cross-axle test, climb a 70% gradient, equivalent to approximately 35 degrees, and wade through water up to 900 mm deep. These capabilities support driving across environments including sand, rough ground, steep slopes and water crossings. Off-road and wading capability remains subject to the vehicle’s operating limits and appropriate driving conditions. International roll-out begins in left-hand drive markets The Middle East is FREELANDER’s strategic starting point for international expansion. The roll-out will proceed in stages, beginning with left-hand drive markets before expanding to right-hand drive and EU specification markets. The international left-hand drive variant will make its dynamic debut at the 2026 Chery International User Summit in Wuhu this October. About FREELANDER FREELANDER is a British Premium Intelligent All-Terrain Brand, jointly developed by JLR and Chery. JLR owns the FREELANDER brand and has established a dedicated FREELANDER Design Hub that leads its design. Chery provides advanced intelligent technology and a top-tier global supply chain. The brand is supported by a strong global foundation, including more than 5,000 employees, five strategic hubs, and fully integrated capabilities spanning design, R&D, manufacturing, and global operations. artigo.texto: Enduro 4 smartwatch redefines ultraperformance with extreme battery life and advanced training features Comprehensive power modes, enhanced stamina metrics, a ComfortFit Fabric Band and Garmin Epic help endurance athletes and multiday adventurers train, race and explore even farther OLATHE, Kan. , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Garmin (NYSE: GRMN) today announced Enduro™ 4, its longest-lasting GPS smartwatch with solar charging, which includes dynamic features and capabilities to take endurance enthusiasts farther on their next expedition. Utilizing an energy-efficient 1.4" MIP display in combination with a solar lens, Enduro 4 has up to 320 hours of battery life in activity mode1 or up to 90 days of battery life in smartwatch mode2. It also leverages innovative updates like grade-adjusted pace-based workout targets, grade-adjusted rolling pace, stamina zones, stamina curve and Garmin Epic multiday activity logging. "As interest and participation in ultra-endurance activities continue to grow, Enduro 4 is designed for athletes and adventurers who want gear they can trust to perform through every mile, every climb and every challenge . Intuitive features like comprehensive power modes make the most of the long-lasting battery life, while grade-adjusted metrics add a new dimension to preparing for hilly or mountainous terrain." —Susan Lyman, Garmin Vice President of Consumer Sales and Marketing Grade-adjusted features, stamina metrics and more In addition to 100+ activity profiles, Enduro 4 introduces new capabilities to the Enduro line, optimized for trail runners, multiday hikers and backpackers, and endurance athletes. - Comprehensive power modes provide preset options to optimize battery life and performance based on the needs of the user. Configurations include Max Accuracy, which offers full-feature tracking for shorter efforts, and Max Battery, ideal for extended activity recording (up to 320 hours with solar charging). - Grade-adjusted pace-based workout targets help athletes maintain the right effort range on hilly terrain, while grade-adjusted rolling pace provides a real-time view of pace over varying terrain. - Stamina zones show athletes how their stamina impacts an activity, and stamina curve helps users understand how their endurance changes over time based on fitness and training history. - With 50% more RAM than Enduro 3 and a more powerful, updated map engine, navigation is easier than ever with 30% faster panning and a smoother, more intuitive map interface for built-in routable maps. Perspective view provides more detail, both close-up and further away, allowing users to better anticipate what comes next. - Garmin Epic allows athletes to combine multiple activities into one cohesive story in Garmin Connect™. Activities can be grouped together over days, weeks or months to create an "Epic", which enables users to add photos and share with family and friends, as well as see health and performance data aggregated during that period. - Enhanced rowing tools provide additional training insights like VO2 max and power curve for indoor rowing activities, while expanded rucking features let users adjust pack weight during an activity and set target metrics like calories burned. Premium design for maximum versatility Enduro 4 weighs in at an incredible 66 grams, making it one of the lightest ultraperformance smartwatches on the market. With a 51mm case, Power Sapphire™ scratch-resistant lens, titanium bezel and lightweight fiber-reinforced polymer case, it is built for the demands of the longest races and most taxing adventures, remaining remarkably light on the wrist. An integrated LED flashlight includes both white and red-light options, while a 10 ATM water resistance rating enables confident use in challenging environments. New to Enduro 4, the ComfortFit Fabric Band combines exceptional comfort, durability and moisture-wicking performance with QuickFit™ functionality, making adjustments and swapping bands even simpler. 64 GB of memory gives users more room for onboard maps, music and data, making it easier to stay prepared for extended adventures away from home. Available now, Enduro 4 has a suggested retail price of $899.99. Learn more at Garmin.com. artigo.texto: FCL-X Fire & Safety to Showcase Advanced Lithium-Ion Battery Fire Protection Solutions at The Battery Show North America 2026 in Detroit - FCL-X Fire & Safety to exhibit atThe Battery Show North America 2026, October 13–15, atHuntington Place inDetroit, Michigan — Booth 1629. - The Company will showcase its proprietary FCL-X™ lithium-ion battery fire extinguishing technology and integrated fire safety solutions for battery manufacturers, electric vehicle OEMs, energy storage operators, and industrial facilities. - Participation follows growing commercial momentum, including the Company's recently announced Integrated Safety Purchase Order with Kia Georgia , supporting its expansion into battery-related safety infrastructure. - The Battery Show offers direct engagement with thousands of engineers, manufacturers, technology providers, and decision-makers across the rapidly expanding North American battery and electrification sectors. TORONTO , Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FCL-X Fire & Safety Inc. ("FFS" or the "Company") (TSXV: FCLX) (OTCQB: FCLIF) (FSE: K0Q), a U.S.-based manufacturer of lithium-ion battery fire safety products and services, is pleased to announce its participation as an exhibitor at The Battery Show North America 2026, taking place October 12–15, 2026, at Huntington Place in Detroit, Michigan. The Company will be exhibiting at Booth 1629 during the exhibition, showcasing its proprietary FCL-X™ lithium-ion battery fire extinguishing technology and expanding portfolio of integrated fire protection and safety solutions. The Battery Show North America is one of the continent's premier gatherings for advanced battery technology, electric vehicles, and energy storage innovation. The 2026 event is expected to bring together more than 16,000 industry professionals, approximately 1,000 exhibitors, and leading representatives from battery manufacturers, automotive OEMs, engineering companies, and technology developers. The Company's participation comes at an important time as the accelerating adoption of lithium-ion batteries across transportation, manufacturing, energy storage, and industrial applications continues to create demand for specialized fire protection technologies and comprehensive safety infrastructure. Building Momentum Across the Battery Safety Industry FCL-X Fire & Safety continues to strengthen its position as a specialized provider of lithium-ion battery fire protection technologies and services. The Company's proprietary FCL-X™ technology is designed to rapidly extinguish lithium-ion battery fires, provide effective cooling, help control thermal runaway, and reduce the risk of reignition. The Company has also broadened its commercial offering beyond fire extinguishing products to include integrated safety services, risk assessment, fire protection engineering, and Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) support for complex battery-related operating environments. Most recently, FCL-X Fire & Safety announced an Integrated Safety Purchase Order with Kia Georgia, Inc., covering construction support and HSE-related services at its West Point, Georgia facility. This engagement represents another important milestone in the Company's evolution toward becoming an integrated safety partner to organizations operating in battery-intensive industries. Carlos Vicens, CEO & Director of FCL-X Fire & Safety, commented: "The Battery Show brings together the companies and decision-makers who are driving the future of electrification. As battery technology advances and deployment accelerates, fire safety must evolve alongside it. We believe that effective lithium-ion battery fire protection is becoming an essential component of battery manufacturing, energy storage, electric vehicle operations, and the broader electrification ecosystem. "Our participation in Detroit provides us with an excellent opportunity to introduce FCL-X™ and our broader safety capabilities directly to the manufacturers, engineers, and operators who are building and managing these critical technologies. Following our recent engagement with Kia Georgia, we are increasingly focused on positioning FCL-X Fire & Safety as an integrated safety solutions partner for the battery industry." Addressing a Critical Challenge in Battery Manufacturing and Electrification Lithium-ion battery fires present significant challenges due to thermal runaway, extreme temperatures, the potential for cell-to-cell propagation, and the risk of reignition. These hazards create operational and infrastructure risks throughout the battery value chain, including production, assembly, testing, transportation, storage, and end-of-life management. As battery manufacturing capacity expands and electric vehicle and battery energy storage system (BESS) installations increase, FCL-X Fire & Safety believes the industry will require a more comprehensive approach to managing these risks. The Company's growing safety platform targets applications across several major sectors: - Battery manufacturing and assembly: Specialized fire protection and safety support for battery production, handling, testing, and storage facilities. - Electric vehicles and automotive OEMs: Lithium-ion battery fire extinguishing technologies and safety services supporting automotive manufacturing, fleet operations, and battery-related facilities. - Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS): Development of advanced suppression technologies, including FCL-X™ GEL, designed to address the unique challenges associated with stationary battery energy storage applications. - Industrial and commercial facilities: Risk assessment, fire protection engineering, HSE services, and fire extinguishing solutions for operations handling lithium-ion batteries. - Transportation, logistics, and recycling: Specialized fire safety technologies for battery storage, handling, transportation, and end-of-life processing. artigo.texto: The technology industry can’t afford to ignore a growing AI data center backlash - Summary: - Concerns over environmental impact but also higher bills for their neighbors is starting to build to real social resentment Just weeks away now, the US midterms have a new factor beyond American voter cost of living or forever war concerns: whether they want what more than a few see as a potential blight on their neighbourhoods - those awful data center things. It seems a lot don't. A recent national Gallup survey reported 70% of Americans oppose data centers being built in their communities, while three-quarters of the 375 data center bills introduced in US state legislatures in 2026 seek to restrict their development in some way. Surprisingly, perhaps, it’s not just the ‘Dumocrats’ doing this: Republican candidates in states including Michigan, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania but most notably Texas, are pushing back on the President’s ‘drill, baby, drill’ pro-AI agenda. You may indeed be a 'socialist dupe’ for not loving all this new compute, but when even Erin Brockovich has set her sights on you, this is not a welcoming climate. There does seem to be a growing case file for the prosecution here: on an almost daily basis, more evidence seems to come out about the downsides of this infrastructure. Meta may be using its US data center buildout as a way to avoid paying at least £4 billion so far in Federal taxes as they are “really” R&D projects, for example, while the push for more and more data center power is driving up fossil fuel demand, nearly tripling gas-fired capacity in the United States in 2025 alone. According to at least one report, Elon Musk is even getting into the turbine-making business himself to keep up. It might not just be the environment that takes a hit from data center building frenzy; investors might soon be feeling the pain as well, given leaked Anthropic IPO plans that suggest it thinks it needs to spend a staggering $518 billion on cloud computing and infrastructure in coming years, despite possibly losing $42 billion last year - with it spending three times on infrastructure in 2025 versus 2024, $7.3 billion. Here, the AI lab’s far from being an outlier: all these guys say they want more and more data centers and more and more juice to run them. But while at least some of the public say they dislike data centers for their perceived negative impact on the water table or pumping out of carbon dioxide, it’s actually their pocketbooks that the real pushback is happening - with headlines about how Google’s proposed data center in West Memphis may ‘have’ to be paid for by a 20-year $6 utility rate hike for locals, as just one example. AI firms and some almond-based whataboutery As so often, the AI firms’ response can seem very tone deaf - like Sam Altman’s claim that 38,000 ChatGPT queries only use as much water, 0.000085 gallons, as “the production of one Californian almond;” the actual figure for the latter, say commentators, is more like 1 to 3.2 gallons, so the ratio is more like 1,000 to 11,000 queries “per almond.” Well, maybe he’s right - but the data center-AI industry isn’t being believed when it says there’s nothing to fear here. Not believed, in fact, to such an extent that, according to a September analysis by Bloomberg, local opposition “blocked or delayed” 45 U.S. data center projects worth approximately $68 billion during the second quarter of 2026. It’s not just US residents raising green fears about all this - UK citizens are also noticing, with reports of how two planned Buckinghamshire and Bedfordshire data centers potentially having higher UK carbon emissions than ExxonMobil - and with 315 more in the queue to connect to the UK’s electricity grid, the argument here, as in the US, is that fossil fuel power is the only thing available so must be used. Last month the Scottish Parliament voted to pause decisions on new AI data centers for up to a year while stricter environmental assessments and national planning guidance are developed - evidence, say activists, of a wider national UK push back against such sites. Which may or not be true, but the sector is in the spotlight. Ofgem, the national UK energy regulator, says applications in the connections queue jumped from 41 GW to 125 GW in less than a year, with data center projects accounting for at least 80 Gigawatts of that. Demand is rising so fast it’s proposing a commitment fee specifically for large data centers so speculative projects don't clog up the grid. The data center industry response So, what to make of all this? Last time we looked in depth at the “AI data centers = the burning up of Planet Earth” equation, the IT industry told us that this was a short-term problem, as renewables would end up being the main power source for all these servers and NVIDIA chips, and anyway, AI would tell us how to run these places more efficiently anyhow. Two years on and in the face of the data center backlash, what is the verdict now? The response falls into two categories: one, that the economic needs for all this are so pressing that we just need to push on, and two, well, we still need to trust that we’ll figure out how to do this more efficiently. In the words of Gary Watson, MD of Stellanor Datacenters: Some level of debate around the growth of data centers is inevitable, particularly as the scale of AI investment increases, but we shouldn’t lose sight of what these facilities actually enable; they are the backbone behind the digital services we use every day, from banking and healthcare to transport and now AI. The answer to concerns about data center growth isn’t to step back from the infrastructure needed to support the digital economy but to think carefully about where they are located and how they connect with the communities around it. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that, as of October 4, 2026, it held 219.9586 Bitcoin representing an aggregate value of approximately $19 million based on the Bitcoin closing price of $86,480. Additionally, the Company held approximately $37.4 million in cash and restricted cash. "We are pleased with the current financial position of the Company," stated Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data. "Our focus remains on strengthening the Company's balance sheet in order to support our core businesses and advance the development of our Michigan AI data center." For more information on Hyperscale Data and its subsidiaries, Hyperscale Data recommends that stockholders, investors and any other interested parties read Hyperscale Data's public filings and press releases available under the Investor Relations section at hyperscaledata.com or available at www.sec.gov. About Hyperscale Data, Inc. Through its wholly owned subsidiary Sentinum, Inc., Hyperscale Data owns and operates a data center at which it offers colocation and hosting services for the emerging AI ecosystems and other industries. Another of Hyperscale Data's wholly owned subsidiaries, Ault Capital Group, Inc. ("ACG"), is a hybrid private equity firm and operating company that acquires, finances, builds and actively manages businesses across financial services, digital assets, industrial services, hospitality, defense technologies and other sectors. Hyperscale Data currently expects the divestiture of ACG (the "Divestiture") to occur in 2027. Upon the occurrence of the Divestiture, the Company would be an owner and operator of data centers to support high-performance computing services, as well as a holder of the digital assets and the third wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Omnipresent Robotics, LLC. Until the Divestiture occurs, the Company will continue to provide, through ACG and its wholly and majority-owned subsidiaries and strategic investments, mission-critical products that support a diverse range of industries, including an AI software platform, equipment rental services, defense/aerospace, industrial, automotive and hotel operations. In addition, ACG is actively engaged in private credit and structured finance through Ault Lending, LLC, a licensed lending subsidiary. Hyperscale Data's headquarters are located at 11411 Southern Highlands Parkway, Suite 190, Las Vegas, NV 89141. On December 23, 2024, the Company issued one million (1,000,000) shares of a newly designated Series F Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the "Series F Preferred Stock") to all common stockholders and holders of the Series C Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis. The Divestiture will occur through the voluntary exchange of the Series F Preferred Stock for shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock of ACG (collectively, the "ACG Shares"). The Company reminds its stockholders that only those holders of the Series F Preferred Stock who agree to surrender such shares, and do not properly withdraw such surrender, in the exchange offer through which the Divestiture will occur, will be entitled to receive the ACG Shares and consequently be shareholders of ACG upon the occurrence of the Divestiture. artigo.texto: Novacium Delivers First Batch of Prototype Batteries to STAT with Twice the Energy Capacity of Batteries Currently in Service - The first batch, delivered to STAT in the third quarter of 2026, integrates GEN3 21700 cylindrical cells in place of the 18650 cells currently in service - With this first delivery, Novacium achieved two key project objectives: - Doubling the energy capacity of the batteries - Limiting geometric modifications to meet dimensional and connector requirements. MONTREAL and SOLAIZE, France, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HPQ Silicon Inc. (TSX-V: HPQ) (OTCQB: HPQFF) (FRA: O08) is pleased to inform its shareholders that its strategic partner, NOVACIUM SAS, a French deep-tech company specializing in green engineering of materials for energy applications, announces that it delivered to the French Army Technical Section ("STAT"), in the third quarter of 2026, a first batch of prototype batteries intended for tactical radio sets. Using its high-capacity cells, Novacium designed batteries offering twice the energy capacity of the batteries currently in service. This delivery follows the award, at the end of June 2026, of a contract by STAT to develop and supply, in successive batches, these high-capacity prototype batteries. Transition to 21700 Cells: Double the Capacity While Preserving Compatibility To achieve this objective, Novacium integrated GEN3 21700 cylindrical cells in place of the previously used 18650 cells. This format offers higher capacity but integrating it required preserving compatibility with existing equipment. Through an optimized cell arrangement and adapted enclosure geometry, Novacium's teams limited dimensional changes to meet STAT's dimensional and connector requirements while doubling the battery's energy capacity. A patent application has been filed for this design. Through the integration of these 21700 cells, the new battery pack reaches an onboard energy capacity of 144 Wh, twice the 72 Wh of the reference battery currently in service, and an energy density of 261 Wh/kg, compared with 160 Wh/kg for the existing solution, representing a 63% increase. An adapted battery management system (BMS), combined with this patent-pending enclosure assembly system, makes the new battery fully compatible with existing connectors, chargers, and interfaces, with only minor changes to its dimensions and mass (42.6 × 98.63 × 74.35 mm; 551 g). Under a comparable usage profile, this doubled energy capacity is intended to provide up to twice the operating time of the reference battery while retaining existing connectors and chargers. STAT will evaluate the operating time actually achieved under operational conditions. An Evaluation Campaign and User Feedback Expected in the Coming Weeks The first batch of prototype batteries delivered in the third quarter of 2026 will undergo an evaluation campaign under operational conditions conducted by STAT. At the end of this phase, detailed feedback (RETEX) will be prepared jointly by STAT and Novacium in the coming weeks. Lessons learned from this field evaluation will allow Novacium to make the necessary design, ergonomic, and parameter-setting adjustments before producing and delivering a second batch that better reflects a production configuration. "Doubling the onboard energy of a tactical radio battery while retaining the existing connectors and chargers represented an engineering challenge that our teams successfully addressed. The transition to 21700 cells enabled us to double the battery's energy capacity, and we worked to limit geometric modifications to preserve compatibility with equipment currently in service. The delivery of this first batch for evaluation under operational conditions is a key milestone: user feedback will guide the adjustments to be made before production of the second batch," said Dr. Jed Kraiem, Ph.D., Chief Operating Officer of Novacium. "The delivery of this first batch illustrates Novacium's ability to transform its anode-material expertise into batteries designed for critical applications," said Bernard Tourillon, President and CEO of HPQ Silicon Inc., which is itself President of Novacium. "If the evaluation phase confirms the expected performance, this program could provide a technical basis for offering the solution to other allied forces with comparable requirements. For HPQ, this program also illustrates the strategic value of our 36.8% interest in Novacium and of its activities in the defence sector." Next Step: A Second Batch Representative of a Production Configuration Following the evaluation campaign and RETEX, Novacium will begin production of a second batch of batteries incorporating lessons learned in the field and better representing a production configuration. This second batch will integrate Novacium's new GEN4 cells, with a capacity exceeding 6,500 mAh, with the objective of increasing the battery's energy capacity at the same mass and therefore its energy density and potential operating time. This stage aims to evaluate the solution's robustness, ergonomics, and reproducibility for potential larger-scale deployment. This first delivery forms part of the expansion of Novacium's activities in the defence and autonomous-systems sectors, notably including the order for battery packs intended for French Army drones, announced on August 19, 2026 through LN'INNOV, and the order for 100 drone battery packs from Alta Ares announced on September 17, 2026. About Novacium SAS Novacium is a French deep-tech company based in Solaize, specializing in developing and producing silicon-based anode materials for lithium-ion batteries through a proprietary process. Novacium also designs custom battery cells and packs for demanding applications, particularly in the defence, aerospace and portable-energy sectors. artigo.texto: e‑STORAGE to Supply and Commission 100 MW/200 MWh Battery Storage System for OX2 in New South Wales KITCHENER, ON , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Canadian Solar Inc. (the "Company" or "Canadian Solar") (NASDAQ: CSIQ) today announced that e‑STORAGE, its energy storage solutions business, has signed an agreement to supply and commission a 100 MW/200 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) for OX2's Muswellbrook Solar Farm and Battery, a solar-plus-storage project in New South Wales, Australia. Shipments are scheduled to begin in Q3 2027, with commercial operation targeted for Q3 2028. The battery cells and SolBank system will be produced in-house at Canadian Solar's manufacturing facilities, giving the customer end-to-end supply chain visibility and ensuring strict quality control across the product. e‑STORAGE will deliver an integrated solution built on SolBank 3.0 battery containers, paired with Power Conversion Systems (PCS), plant controls, and the Company's proprietary EQ-S Energy Management System (EMS) developed and built in-house by e‑STORAGE's North American software team. e‑STORAGE will be responsible for the R1 grid connection studies, supply the hybrid power plant controller that coordinates the battery with the co-located solar farm, and lead the overall integration and commissioning of the hybrid project. The arrangement is backed by a 20-year long-term service agreement (LTSA), placing hardware, proprietary software, and long-term performance under a single accountable partner. The project sits roughly 2.5 kilometers east of Muswellbrook, on land at a former coal mine within the Hunter-Central Coast Renewable Energy Zone. The location is significant: as the region's aging coal generators wind down toward retirement in the early 2030s, the dispatchable capacity they once provided must be replaced. Two-hour storage fills that gap directly, holding midday solar output and releasing it into the evening demand peak when supply from retiring thermal plants tightens. Once operational, the system will support the long-term hybrid power purchase agreement OX2 has signed for the project, converting variable solar output into firm, contracted supply. By storing and dispatching solar energy on demand, the BESS strengthens grid reliability in a region transitioning away from coal and helps deliver firm renewable power to the communities in the Hunter Region. Steve Symons, Vice President, OX2 Australia, said: "This battery storage system is what turns Muswellbrook into a true hybrid facility — pairing solar generation with storage so we can capture energy when the sun is shining and deliver it when the grid needs it most. It's a key step in providing firm, reliable renewable power to the Hunter region." Jeff Roy, President of e ‑ STORAGE, said: "Australia's energy transition is being decided in regions like the Hunter, where storage now has to carry the load that retiring coal once did. We control this project from the cell through to our own energy management software and 20 years of service, which means OX2 has one partner accountable for how the system performs over its full life." About Canadian Solar Inc. Canadian Solar is one of the world's largest solar technology and renewable energy companies. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Kitchener, Ontario, the Company is a leading manufacturer of solar photovoltaic modules; provider of solar energy and battery energy storage solutions; and developer, owner, and operator of utility-scale solar power and battery energy storage projects. Over the past 25 years, Canadian Solar has successfully delivered nearly 180 GW of premium-quality solar photovoltaic modules to customers across the world. Through its energy storage solutions business e-STORAGE, Canadian Solar has shipped over 23 GWh of battery energy storage solutions to global markets and had a contracted backlog of $3.5 billion as of June 30, 2026. Since entering the project development business in 2010, Canadian Solar has developed, built, and connected approximately 12.4 GWp of solar power projects and 6.4 GWh of battery energy storage projects globally. Its geographically diversified project development pipeline includes approximately 22 GWp of solar and 84 GWh of battery energy storage capacity in various stages of development. Canadian Solar is one of the most bankable companies in the solar and renewable energy industry, having been publicly listed on the NASDAQ since 2006. For additional information about the Company, follow Canadian Solar on LinkedIn or visit www.canadiansolar.com. About e-STORAGE e-STORAGE is a subsidiary of Canadian Solar and a leading company specializing in designing, manufacturing, and integrating battery energy storage systems for utility-scale applications. e-STORAGE offers proprietary battery energy storage systems (BESS) spanning battery cells, battery PACKs, power conversion systems (PCS), energy management systems (EMS) and system integration. It also provides comprehensive EPC services and full-lifecycle station operation and asset management, helping customers improve grid operations across the project lifecycle. For more info, please refer to the Media&PR section of www.csestorage.com and follow our LinkedIn page. artigo.texto: RMX Publishes Brief on QuantrusX Distributed Data Center DALLAS , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RMX Industries, Inc. (OTCQB: RMXI), a Real-World Intelligence company, today announced the publication of Part Three of its brief series on Real-World Intelligence, the Company's name for intelligence built at the physical edge ("RWI"), examining the QuantrusX™ Distributed Data Center ("QXDDC") and RMX's intended approach to connecting on-site computing deployments. Building on the first two briefs' examination of RWI and QuantrusX™ at individual facilities, the new publication explains how connected QuantrusX™ nodes are intended to learn from one another through a distributed intelligence fabric, helping each site interpret activity and respond more effectively while preserving data sovereignty and operator authority over response decisions. "We believe the value of connected intelligence should be measured by how well it helps people respond at their own sites," said Karl Kit, CEO of RMX. "With QXDDC, our intent is for each QuantrusX™ deployment to benefit from learning across the fabric while keeping the site's data under the site's control and response decisions with the people responsible for the operation." Part Three is available to read on the Company's website: https://rmx.io/news/qxddc-real-world-intelligence-connected-across-the-physical-world. About RMX: RMX Industries, Inc. ("RMX" or the "Company") (OTCQB: RMXI) is a Real-World Intelligence company. Real-World Intelligence is the Company's name for intelligence built at the physical edge. Through QuantrusX™, its proprietary edge intelligence platform, RMX brings intelligence to the physical world so operators can interpret data faster, respond locally, and decide with confidence where connectivity, time, and context matter. For more information, visit www.rmx.io. artigo.texto: Cheche Group (NASDAQ: CCG) Advances "Green Mobility + Green Energy" Strategy with Proposed Move into Home Energy Storage HONG KONG, Oct 9, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - Cheche Group Inc. (NASDAQ: CCG) is pursuing an expansion into residential battery storage and home energy management under its 'Green Mobility + Green Energy' two-pillar strategy. The planned expansion would complement its established NEV insurance technology business and support its broader 'Car + Home' vision. Cheche's existing platform connects automakers and insurance carriers to support digital insurance transactions and services. In the first half of 2026, its NEV partnerships generated approximately 1.0 million insurance policies, up 29.5% from a year earlier. Corresponding written premiums rose 23.7% to RMB3.2 billion. The company had partnerships with 18 NEV manufacturers as of June 30, 2026. This business has given Cheche experience in integrating insurance services into automakers' customer channels. Its technology supports insurance transactions, pricing and claims processes through data integration and risk modeling. For the proposed home energy expansion, Cheche is targeting Long Way Fortune, a residential energy technology provider operating under its brand EnergyLIB. Long Way Fortune brings hardware engineering, modular battery products, and local service capabilities. Its portfolio includes modular batteries and hybrid inverters designed for both retrofit solar-plus-storage and new installations. The business operates in Australia and Singapore, with a model that includes local distribution, installation support and after-sales service. EnergyLIB is also developing home energy management functions that use electricity consumption, solar generation, weather, tariffs and battery operating data. These functions are intended to help households manage electricity costs while accounting for backup power needs and battery usage. Cheche sees a potential role for its insurance technology and business relationships in services around these energy assets, and will explore potential insurance and financing solutions that could help spread customers' upfront payments over time. These offerings remain in the planning stage and would require product development and partner arrangements. The strategic roadmap prioritizes Australia as the initial market, emphasizing local delivery and after-sales support while building towards broader synergies across the EV and green energy value chains, where solar generates power, storage optimizes it, software manages it, and NEVs consume it. Cheche is pursuing the expansion through a proposed strategic investment in Long Way Fortune, bringing together its insurance technology expertise with EnergyLIB's residential storage solutions to advance the broader "Car + Home" green ecosystem. artigo.texto: Community hears updates on Swatara Township data centers Plans for two hyperscale data centers in Swatara Township, Dauphin County, were presented during a community meeting, drawing mixed reactions from local residents. Community hears updates on Swatara Township data centers Plans for two hyperscale data centers in Swatara Township, Dauphin County, were presented during a community meeting, drawing mixed reactions from local residents. Developers presented plans for two 'hyperscale data centers' in Swatara Township, Dauphin County, during a community info session Thursday night. One project leader says a data center could be up and running as soon as 2028. $10.5 billion campus planned across two sites The project, backed by Corscale, is divided into two parts, but developers described it as one large campus. The Dauphin Highlands Golf Course, which is expected to close on October 12th, will be the site of the "Highlands West" portion of the project. Developers say that portion will span 228 acres and will include three buildings. Across the highway, near Highland Street and Grayson Road, the other portion will be called "Highlands East." Developers say it will cover 156 acres and feature two buildings. The entire project is estimated to cost roughly 10.5 billion dollars. Thursday's session allowed attendees to speak directly with project leaders, including Erik Draaisma, Corscale’s executive vice president of business development. "A lot of [data center] projects are being spun up as speculative. This is no such project," Draaisma told WGAL on Thursday. "We think it's going to be an excellent development. We fit well within all the ordinances. We're excited to get it going." Developers address water, power and neighborhood concerns A major focus of the meeting was Corscale’s commitment to building 'responsible data centers,' according to developers. Draaisma explained that the centers will use closed-loop cooling systems, consuming about as much water as an office building does daily. "And if people are worried about contamination of groundwater, we don't touch the groundwater. There's not a well system. We're drawing it from the municipality, and we're discharging it to the municipalities, like anyone else," Draaisma said. Additionally, Draaisma said Corscale plans to invest millions into local power infrastructure. Developers also outlined plans to address traffic concerns, maintain distance between the buildings and nearby neighborhoods, and reduce noise pollution from the centers. Draaisma emphasized Corscale’s intention to contribute positively to the community. "I fully understand that development is not necessarily something that everyone wants, especially if you're nearby. It is, however, very important to keep your people employed, to keep your economy moving and for your municipalities to deliver services that you rely on," Draaisma said. Community reaction still mixed Both sites are near residential neighborhoods, prompting varied reactions from residents who attended the meeting. Some people WGAL spoke with said they are still undecided on the project. Others, however, remain unconvinced. "I'm completely against it. I think it's terrible," Thomas White said. "No matter what these posters say, they're just trying to sell it to you in the nicest way. No matter what, it's a strain on our utilities, on our services, on our air pollution, and on our noise pollution. I don't see a single benefit." Nick McDade, another nearby resident, expressed similar concerns, questioning the value of the $120 million community benefit agreement signed by Swatara Township on Wednesday. "What's the point of having all this money if I can't live here? You know, if there's dirty air or dirty water, what's the money going to do for me?" McDade said. "I'm not a big fan of it, and they're trying to put them up all over. It affects the firemen, the water, the temperature of the air, everything." Developers stated that groundbreaking for the project could begin in 2027, with the data centers potentially operational by 2028 or 2029. However, they noted that additional approvals, including design approvals, are still required before construction can proceed.

artigo.texto: Commentary: Data Centers Aren’t the Only Threat to Farmland by Tim Gibbons / National Family Farm Coalition and Dena Hoff / Northern Plains Resource Council, The Daily Yonder Protests against data centers have exploded across the US, with communities revolting against a multitude of proven damaging effects on energy prices, clean air and water – and the devastation of tens of thousands of acres of agricultural land. Recent headlines in national publications report that farmers and rural communities are rejecting multimillion-dollar bids from institutional investors and tech companies to buy their farmland to build data centers. A farmer in Kentucky rejected $33 million for her farmland; another in Pennsylvania turned down a $15 million offer; and one farmer in Wisconsin even reportedly refused a whopping $70+ million bid. Land has become the next big asset class for investors, especially billionaires and private equity firms, to hide and protect their wealth. It is seen as a safe, low-risk way to park money to hedge against inflation – at the expense of farmers and local communities alike. These investors aren’t just seeking out farmland to build data centers. Just like they’re targeting housing, investment firms are buying up land and renting it back to farmers for a hefty profit. The 2024 Tenure, Ownership, and Transition of Agricultural Land (TOTAL) Survey, released this March, shows that 87% of the more than 2 million landowners renting out farmland are non-operators – that is, they are not actively farming, and the majority of these landowners never have. While these landlords raked in more than $34 billion in rent combined, the total value of farmland held for rent is $1.7 trillion – up 47% since 2014. We are watching in real time the emergence of a long-term, non-farming rural landlord class. While the TOTAL survey provides a useful indicator of farmland ownership trends, it doesn’t give us the full picture. Farmland ownership has never been effectively tracked in the US with regularity, and what limited data exists is difficult to find. The data we do have shows that investment in farmland has risen dramatically over the past two decades. Companies like AcreTrader, Farmland Partners, and others that allow individuals to invest in farmland have become increasingly popular. The most alarming growth has come from institutional investors, like pension funds, private equity firms, and wealth management groups. The value of farmland held by institutional investors has more than doubled over the past three years up to $16.6 billion dollars by 2024, an eightfold rise since 2008. Based on publicly available data alone, the largest corporate owners of US farmland control more than 2 million acres. But why are farmers selling their land in the first place? The hard truth is that farming just isn’t working as a viable livelihood anymore, and hasn’t for years. In just five years from 2017-2022, we lost 159,000 US family farms. The Farm Crisis didn’t go away in the 1980s – it’s just become quieter and less visible to most. Chronic low and volatile prices across sectors, coupled with a handful of multinational corporations tightening their iron grip over global agriculture, have pushed farmers to the brink of existence. With farm debt at an all-time high, selling the farm for the best offer possible is often the only feasible way to escape dire financial straits. And when the farm is for sale, companies with billions in assets are primed to outbid new and beginning farmers seeking land to start their own businesses. The best opportunity we have to protect farmland comes from strong federal policies that safeguard land for multiple generations of working farms and ensure farmers make a living wage. Right now, the Farmland for Farmers Act is one of the boldest pieces of federal legislation to combat this worrying trend. Modeled after anti-corporate farming laws in Midwestern states, the bill would stop large corporate entities from being able to purchase farmland only to let it lie fallow in the hopes that its value will skyrocket over time, or to rent it back to farmers at a premium price. With policies like it, coupled with a Farm Bill that allows farmers to pay their bills and sustainably grow their businesses, farmers might stand a chance. It’s long overdue for policy solutions championed by federal representatives not afraid to stand up against deep pocketed special interests. We need Congress to enact policies like the Farmland for Farmers Act that fight back against the profiteering on the backs of farmers, communities, and our natural resources. The first step in protecting farmland means supporting the next generation of farmers to enter the business with confidence and without having to compete with billionaires. We need to ensure that farmers now and in the future actually have the land they need to feed us all. Tim Gibbons is the Executive Director of the National Family Farm Coalition, a national coalition representing 30 grassroots farm, ranch, and fishing organizations in Washington, DC. A life-long Missourian, Tim has spent decades organizing family farmers, ranchers, and rural residents in support of fair, healthy and thriving rural economies, fair markets, and clean water and air. Dena Hoff represents the Northern Plains Resource Council on the NFFC Board. Since 1979, she’s raised sheep, cattle, alfalfa, corn, and edible dry beans, among other crops, on her farm in Glendive, Montana. She is an active member of and advocate for her rural community. This article first appeared on The Daily Yonder and is republished here under a Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License.

artigo.texto: Juscelino põe postes, Fust e data centers na agenda do novo mandato Deputado e ex-ministro das Comunicações diz que pretende avançar com regras de compartilhamento de postes, recursos do Fust e infraestrutura para data centers O deputado federal Juscelino Filho, ex-ministro das Comunicações, colocou a regulamentação do compartilhamento de postes, a proteção dos recursos do Fust e a infraestrutura necessária à expansão dos data centers entre as prioridades de sua atuação no Congresso nos próximos anos. Reeleito para o quarto mandato, Juscelino afirmou na abertura da Futurecom 2026, nesta terça-feira, 6, em São Paulo, que pretende manter a agenda de telecomunicações e infraestrutura digital como uma das frentes de atuação parlamentar. O deputado preside a Frente Parlamentar de Telecomunicações e Soluções Digitais e disse que o grupo pretende atuar para dar continuidade às políticas do setor independentemente das mudanças no comando do governo federal. “É muito importante a gente ser vigilante”, afirmou ao tratar da continuidade dos investimentos. Segundo ele, a frente deverá trabalhar para garantir que políticas de Estado tenham sequência “independente de presidente que seja”. Relatório sobre postes deve ser apresentado Entre as pautas legislativas citadas está o PL 3.220/2019, que trata do compartilhamento de postes entre os setores elétrico e de telecomunicações e tem Juscelino como relator na Câmara. O deputado afirmou que ouviu empresas, entidades e especialistas dos dois setores e que pretende apresentar “em breve” seu relatório. A regulamentação dos postes é uma discussão de longa duração entre telecomunicações e distribuição de energia, envolvendo ocupação, preço, regularização das redes e responsabilidades das empresas que utilizam a infraestrutura. Fust volta ao centro da disputa orçamentária Juscelino também voltou a defender mecanismos que impeçam o contingenciamento dos recursos do Fundo de Universalização dos Serviços de Telecomunicações. Em seu discurso, lembrou que o Fust passou a financiar projetos de infraestrutura depois de mais de duas décadas de existência e citou aplicações em redes de fibra, escolas, áreas rurais e comunidades. O ex-ministro defendeu a continuidade dessa utilização e afirmou que o Congresso precisa garantir os recursos necessários aos investimentos. A questão também apareceu no quebra-queixo com Frederico. O atual ministro confirmou que existe uma discussão dentro do governo sobre restrições aos recursos e disse estar negociando com outras áreas do Executivo para preservar investimentos em infraestrutura digital. Redata é apenas uma etapa, diz Juscelino Na agenda de data centers, Juscelino afirmou que a aprovação do Redata representa um passo para atrair novos investimentos, mas relacionou o desenvolvimento desse mercado a uma infraestrutura mais ampla. Em sua intervenção, mencionou a necessidade de redes robustas, cabos submarinos, fibra óptica, energia e instrumentos de financiamento. “Não adianta você só ter o data center em algum lugar se você não tiver uma rede robusta, se você não tiver conectividade, velocidade, para esses dados estarem trafegando”, afirmou. O deputado também apontou a regulamentação do Redata como a próxima etapa e observou que, depois dela, haverá a discussão do ICMS com os governos estaduais. A avaliação converge com a posição apresentada pelo governo de São Paulo na Futurecom: o estado pretende discutir a adequação de sua tributação depois da regulamentação federal. Continuidade das políticas entra no debate A diferença entre a fala de Juscelino e as manifestações mais institucionais da abertura está na preocupação explícita com a continuidade das políticas públicas após a próxima mudança de ciclo político. O deputado defendeu que investimentos em conectividade e infraestrutura digital sejam tratados como políticas permanentes, independentemente de quem ocupe a Presidência. A agenda apresentada por Juscelino reúne, assim, questões que estão em diferentes estágios: o Redata já passou pelo Congresso e depende de regulamentação; o compartilhamento de postes continua em tramitação; e a proteção dos recursos do Fust permanece vinculada às decisões legislativas e orçamentárias. Para o setor de telecomunicações, essas três frentes deverão ocupar parte relevante da agenda do Congresso no encerramento de 2026 e no início da próxima legislatura.

artigo.texto: Judge dismisses lawsuit challenging $2.8B Valara data center in S.C. SPARTANBURG COUNTY, S.C. (WRDW/WAGT) - A judge has thrown out a lawsuit that sought to block permits for Valara Holdings’ $2.8 billion data center in South Carolina. The group Concerned Citizens of Spartanburg County argued the county broke its own rules by approving the project as a “minor” development, which gets staff-only review with no public hearing. They said a project this big should have gone through “major” review, with public notice, public comment and a Planning Commission vote. Judge J. Derham Cole Jr. threw the case out Oct. 6 for two reasons: - No specific harm shown: The judge said concerns about noise, dust, traffic, transparency and health were too general. Under state law, neighbors must show they were “specially damaged” to block a project. - Wrong process: The judge said the group should have appealed to the county’s Board of Zoning Appeals within 10 days first, before going to court. He also said the fight over the second permit is too early because the county hasn’t decided on it yet. That second application — for four new buildings, a power yard and cooling systems, is still pending. The first permit to redevelop the old Kohler plant was approved in August 2025. The ruling also ends the group’s bid to pause construction. A judge heard that pause request Sept. 17 and took it under advisement. In August, state regulators dismissed a separate challenge over Valara’s plans for gas turbines to power the site. In June, Spartanburg County paused new data center applications for one year, but that does not stop Valara, which was already underway. Read the order in full: Copyright 2026 WRDW/WAGT. A Finlândia ordenou que a Google (GOOGL) pare os trabalhos em dois data centers de IA. A ordem é um revés para a ação da Alphabet, vindo apenas um mês após a empresa prometer US$ 15 bilhões para infraestrutura de IA no país. A Agência de Licenciamento e Supervisão (LVV) da Finlândia enviou a notificação à subsidiária da Google, Tuike Finland Oy. Ela abrange projetos planejados em Muhos e Kajaani. Os trabalhos devem parar até que as avaliações de impacto ambiental sejam concluídas. O prazo é 23 de outubro. A ordem cobre remoção de árvores, escavação, extração de pedra, abertura de valas e construção de estradas. O planejamento, medições e levantamentos de solo podem continuar, pois têm apenas impactos menores. Tommi Muilu, chefe de assuntos ambientais da agência, disse que o trabalho alteraria o meio ambiente. Ele afirmou que identificar esses impactos é um objetivo fundamental do processo de avaliação. A Google disse que não cumpriu seus próprios padrões. Também afirmou que agiu de boa fé sob a Lei Florestal e seguirá as orientações da agência. A empresa planeja plantar árvores em 130 hectares (320 acres) em Muhos. O plano de US$ 15 bilhões seria o maior investimento da Google na Europa. A empresa gastará o dinheiro até 2028 em data centers e projetos de energia. A Finlândia se tornou um ponto quente para data centers porque tem terra e energia disponíveis. A administração também espera que o capex aumente significativamente em 2027. Gastos dessa magnitude deixam pouco espaço para atrasos. O fluxo de caixa livre no 2º trimestre foi negativo em US$ 5,9 bilhões. Qualquer pausa em um local de data center pode retardar a velocidade com que nova capacidade entra em operação. Ainda assim, a ordem cobre apenas dois projetos e termina assim que as revisões forem concluídas. A Google afirmou que cumprirá. artigo.texto: NY Senate candidates spar over AI data centers, immigration law PLATTSBURGH, N.Y. (WCAX) - Candidates in New York’s 45th Senate District met in a debate on Tuesday, with incumbent Republican Dan Stec facing Glens Falls nurse practitioner and Democrat Melissa Seale ahead of the November election. A panel asked the candidates several questions, including their thoughts on New York’s one-year AI data center moratorium. “If there’s adequate energy there, then why shouldn’t it go forward? That should be a decision that’s made locally and not from Albany, which is why I opposed the moratorium,” Stec said. “The biggest thing is making sure these AI data centers do not impact our communities, the people and the environment,” Seale said. Both candidates also provided their views on statewide immigration policy. Debate panel member Alek LaShomb: Local Cops, Local Crimes Act passed this year that prohibits local law enforcement from working with federal immigration officials on civil investigations. Do you think this legislation goes far enough or would you like to see this peeled back a little bit? Melissa Seale: If we are having our community police officers do the work of immigration, which is a federal program, it’s taking away from our communities and I feel it could make them less safe. Dan Stec: You do not want cops knowing one thing and their brothers and sisters in law enforcement having any ability to work with each other; it’s just unsafe for everybody. Stec and Seale also said they would work to get a constitutional amendment on former state prisons to voters. That proposal would take three vacant state prisons out of the forest preserve and make them available for development. “We have a housing crisis; how can we be creative in utilizing these facilities?” Seale said. While Seale said she doesn’t know how much land should be exchanged for the trio, Stec said he would compromise on a higher amount. Alek LaShomb: If environmentalists say we want more than two thousand acres for all three back into the forest preserve, would you support that? Dan Stec: Yes, I would like to know what exactly we are talking about as far as what 2000 acres that is as I am sure they would, but there’s no magic number for me. Mountain Lake PBS’ full debate airs Friday, Oct. 9 at 8 p.m. You can also watch online and on the PBS app. Election Day is Nov. 3. Copyright 2026 WCAX. All rights reserved.
